meta.inflation_note: İsviçre şirketleri enflasyon muhasebesi uygulamaz. Bu yüzden bütün şirketlerin özsermaye kârlılığı yıl sonu tüketici enflasyonuyla düzeltildi: 2021 için %1,5, 2022 için %2,8, 2023 için %1,7, 2024 için %0,6, 2025 için %0,1. Son 12 ay için en son açıklanan yıllık oran (Ekim 2026, %1,5) kullanıldı.
data_notes: Fiyat, piyasa değeri, F/K ve PD/DD: TradingView tarayıcısı, 13 Kasım 2026 kapanışı. Evren 205 paydır: 200'ü SIX Swiss Exchange'te, 5'i BX Swiss'te. Ana kotasyonu başka ülkede olan paylar evrende yoktur; evrendeki 2 yatırım ortaklığı 1. surda dışarıda kalır.

Karşılaştırma: SIX'in kendi tanıtım yayını borsada '220'den fazla kote şirket' olduğunu yazıyor (tarihsiz; içeriği 2025 sonuna ait). Dünya Bankası'nın WFE'ye dayanan sayısı 2021 için 220 yerli şirkettir. Evrenin SIX bölümü (200) bu sayının yaklaşık %9 altında. Tarihli ve yerli-yabancı ayrımlı resmî bir sayı bu çalıştırmada açılamadı.

Denetim (15 Kasım 2026): Roche, Novartis, Nestlé, ABB ve UBS'te fiyat 13 Kasım kapanışıyla aynı, piyasa değeri ikinci kaynakla %4 içinde. Novartis'te F/K iki kaynakta farklı (evrende 32,3; ikinci kaynakta yaklaşık 25): ikinci kaynağın sayfası üçüncü çeyrekten önceye aitti; o çeyrekte net kâr 1,9 milyar dolarlık bir değer düşüklüğüyle 1,2 milyar dolara indi. Toplayıcının hesapladığı F/K, Berner Kantonalbank'ta 23,82 (banka kârlarıyla yaklaşık 23,7), Glarner Kantonalbank'ta 14,50 (14,50). PD/DD, Temenos'ta 16,0 (30 Haziran 2026 özsermayesiyle yaklaşık 17,6).

Şirketin belgesiyle düzeltilen (15 Kasım 2026). Georg Fischer: kaynak PD/DD'yi azınlık payları dahil toplam özsermayeyle (27 milyon frank) hesaplayıp 177 buluyordu. Şirketin 30 Haziran 2026 bilançosunda ana ortaklığa ait özsermaye eksi 23 milyon frank; şirket Swiss GAAP FER uygular ve şerefiyeyi özsermayeden düşer. Şirket ayrıca son 12 ayda zararda olduğu için 1. surda kalır.

Swiss GAAP FER uygulayan şirketler (örnek: SFS, Emmi, Georg Fischer) satın almalardan doğan şerefiyeyi özsermayeden düşebilir. Bu, özsermayeyi küçültür; özsermaye kârlılığını ve PD/DD'yi yükseltir. Süzgeç kaynağın rakamını olduğu gibi kullanır; okunan şirketlerde bu durum raporda yazar.

Roche'un beş yıllık oran sayfası gelmedi (kaynak sayfayı hamiline pay kodu RO ile vermiyor). Roche bu yüzden 2. surda 'veri eksik' diye durur; bu, kalitesinin ölçüldüğü anlamına gelmez. BB Biotech ve Procimmo da aynı durumda. Evrende Roche'un yalnız hamiline payı (RO) vardır; piyasa değeri bütün pay sınıflarını kapsar.

Veri kaynağı 6 şirkette son 12 ayın kârını vermiyor: Bajaj Mobility, DocMorris, Centiel, Matador Secondary Private Equity, Xlife Sciences ve MindMaze Therapeutics. Bu şirketler kaynakta kâr verisi olmadığı için değerlendirilemedi. Kaynağın PD/DD alanı boş olan 5 şirkette PD/DD aynı kaynağın bilanço alanlarından tamamlandı.

Novartis, ABB, UBS, Logitech, Temenos, Accelleron ve INFICON gibi şirketler tablolarını ABD dolarıyla açıklar; payları frankla işlem görür. Oranlar para biriminden bağımsızdır; enflasyon düzeltmesi İsviçre enflasyonuyla yapıldı. Çoğu İsviçre şirketi yılda iki kez bilanço açıklar.

Beş yıllık oranlar: stockanalysis.com oran sayfaları; 59 adayın 56'sının sayfası geldi. Yıl sonu enflasyonu: İsviçre Federal İstatistik Ofisi (BFS), tüketici fiyat endeksi (LIK), aralık ayı yıllık oranları (2021-2025). Son yıllık oran: BFS, Ekim 2026 (%1,5).

2. suru geçen 24 şirketin hepsi okundu (15 Kasım 2026): 20'si 3. suru geçti, 4'ü hendek ölçütünde kaldı (Kuehne+Nagel, SFS, Emmi, Burkhalter). Kale yok: 3. suru geçenlerin hepsinde fiyat temkinli değerin üstünde. Swissquote'un son 12 ay kârının yaklaşık %14'ü tek seferlik kazançtı (Yuh payının yeniden değerlemesi) ve kazanç yargısında düşüldü.

en.inflation_note: Swiss companies do not apply inflation accounting. The return on equity of every company was therefore adjusted by year-end consumer inflation: 1.5% for 2021, 2.8% for 2022, 1.7% for 2023, 0.6% for 2024 and 0.1% for 2025. For the last 12 months the most recently published annual rate (October 2026, 1.5%) was used.
data_notes: Price, market value, P/E and P/B: TradingView screener, close of 13 November 2026. The universe is 205 stocks: 200 on SIX Swiss Exchange and 5 on BX Swiss. Stocks whose main listing is in another country are not in the universe; the 2 investment companies that are in it stay outside at Wall 1.

For comparison: SIX's own brochure says the exchange has 'over 220 listed companies' (undated; its content refers to the end of 2025). The World Bank's number, based on WFE, is 220 domestic companies for 2021. The SIX part of the universe (200) is about 9% below that number. A dated official count split into domestic and foreign companies could not be opened in this run.

Checks (15 November 2026): for Roche, Novartis, Nestlé, ABB and UBS the price equals the close of 13 November and market value agrees with a second source within 4%. For Novartis the P/E differs between the two sources (32.3 in the universe, about 25 in the second source): the second source's page predates the third quarter, in which net profit fell to 1.2 billion dollars after an impairment of 1.9 billion dollars. The P/E calculated by the collector is 23.82 for Berner Kantonalbank (about 23.7 with the bank's profits) and 14.50 for Glarner Kantonalbank (14.50). P/B is 16.0 for Temenos (about 17.6 with equity at 30 June 2026).

Corrected with the company's own document (15 November 2026). Georg Fischer: the source calculated P/B on total equity including minority interests (27 million francs) and showed 177. In the company's balance sheet of 30 June 2026, equity attributable to shareholders is minus 23 million francs; the company reports under Swiss GAAP FER and offsets goodwill against equity. The company is also loss-making over the last 12 months, so it stays at Wall 1.

Companies reporting under Swiss GAAP FER (for example SFS, Emmi, Georg Fischer) may offset goodwill from acquisitions against equity. This shrinks equity and raises return on equity and P/B. The funnel uses the source's figure as it is; for the companies that were read, the report says so.

Roche's five-year ratio page did not arrive (the source does not serve the page under the bearer-share code RO). Roche therefore stands at Wall 2 as 'data missing'; this does not mean its quality was measured. BB Biotech and Procimmo are in the same position. The universe holds only Roche's bearer share (RO); its market value covers all share classes.

For 6 companies the data source gives no profit figure for the last 12 months: Bajaj Mobility, DocMorris, Centiel, Matador Secondary Private Equity, Xlife Sciences and MindMaze Therapeutics. These companies could not be assessed because the source has no profit data. For 5 companies where the source's P/B field is empty, P/B was completed from the same source's balance-sheet fields.

Companies such as Novartis, ABB, UBS, Logitech, Temenos, Accelleron and INFICON report in US dollars while their shares trade in francs. Ratios do not depend on the currency; the inflation adjustment uses Swiss inflation. Most Swiss companies publish a balance sheet twice a year.

Five-year ratios: stockanalysis.com ratio pages; the pages of 56 of the 59 candidates arrived. Year-end inflation: Swiss Federal Statistical Office (FSO), consumer price index (CPI), December annual rates (2021-2025). Latest annual rate: FSO, October 2026 (1.5%).

All 24 companies that passed Wall 2 have been read (15 November 2026): 20 passed Wall 3 and 4 failed the moat test (Kuehne+Nagel, SFS, Emmi, Burkhalter). There is no castle: for every company that passed Wall 3 the price is above the conservative value. About 14% of Swissquote's profit for the last 12 months was a one-off gain (remeasurement of its Yuh stake) and was deducted in the earnings judgment.

TEMN.one: Bankalara ana bankacılık yazılımı satar; gelirinin çoğu yinelenir. Hendek dar. Özsermaye geri alımlarla küçüldüğü için kârlılık oranı olduğundan yüksek görünür.
TEMN.business: Temenos bankalara ana bankacılık yazılımı satar: hesapları, kredileri ve ödemeleri işleten çekirdek sistem. Parayı abonelik ve bulut (SaaS) ücretlerinden, bakım sözleşmelerinden ve kurulum hizmetinden kazanır. 2025'te gelir 1.090,8 milyon dolar, faaliyet kârı 248,0 milyon dolar oldu. 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreğinde gelirin 121,8 milyon doları abonelik ve SaaS, 134,7 milyon doları bakım, 36,2 milyon doları hizmetti. Yıllık yinelenen gelir (ARR) 903,6 milyon dolar. Şirket dolar ile raporlar; hisse İsviçre frangıyla işlem görür.
TEMN.moat_text: Hendek dar sınıfta. Kanıt: ana bankacılık sistemi bankanın bütün işlemlerini taşır; değiştirmek yıllar süren, riskli bir projedir. Bu yüzden gelir yinelenir: ARR 903,6 milyon dolar, son 12 ayın gelirinin (1.141,6 milyon dolar) yaklaşık %79'u. ARR bir yılda %11 arttı. Reel özsermaye kârlılığı beş yılda ortalama %31,3, en düşük yılında %18,4. Neden geniş değil: bu oran özsermayenin geri alımlarla küçülmesinden de gelir (özsermaye 2024 sonunda 639,0 milyon dolardı, Haziran 2026'da 372,0 milyon dolar); yatırılan sermayenin getirisi daha düşüktür (son okuma %20,8). Müşteri kaybı da görülüyor: tek bir "şimdi al sonra öde" müşterisinin ayrılması 2026'da ARR büyümesinden 3 puan, abonelik gelirinden 5 puan götürüyor. Büyük bir sözleşmenin birkaç gün kayması çeyrek hedefini kaçırtıyor (üçüncü çeyrek: hedef en az %30, gerçekleşen %22). Brüt marjın enflasyon yıllarındaki seyrine bakıldı; okunan belgelerde yok.
TEMN.mgmt: Kâr temettüye ve geri alıma gidiyor; borç da artıyor. 2025'te 320,4 milyon dolarlık kendi payı alındı. 2026'nın ilk yarısında 114,2 milyon dolarlık pay alındı (1.244.986 pay, 89,8 milyon frank; pay başına yaklaşık 72 frank) ve 117,9 milyon dolar temettü ödendi (hisse başına 1,40 frank). 2026 genel kurulu 3.952.656 payı iptal etti. 13 Ağustos 2026'da 100 milyon franka kadar yeni bir geri alım başladı; alınan paylar çalışan pay planları ve satın almalar için tutulacak. Hisse bazlı ücret yüksek: ilk yarıda 24,6 milyon dolar, dönem kârının (107,0 milyon dolar) %23'ü. Şirketin "non-IFRS" kârı bunu dışarıda bırakır; o ölçüye güvenmiyoruz. Yeniden yapılanma gideri her dönem var (ilk yarı 2026: 8,0 milyon dolar; ilk yarı 2025: 25,8 milyon dolar); olağan gider sayıyoruz. additiv 17 Temmuz 2026'da alındı (ön bedel 226,7 milyon frank). Maddi olmayan varlıklar 1.259,9 milyon dolar, özsermayenin üç katından fazla; şerefiye ayrı verilmemiş. Emeklilik ve bilanço dışı yükümlülüklere, ortaklık yapısına bakıldı; okunan belgelerde yok.
TEMN.latest: 27 Ekim 2026: Şirket üçüncü çeyrek sonuçlarını açıkladı. Gelir 292,5 milyon dolar (bir yıl önce 258,5), faaliyet kârı 84,8 milyon dolar (60,1), net kâr 63,4 milyon dolar (44,4), seyreltilmiş hisse başına kâr 0,92 dolar (0,65). ARR 903,6 milyon dolar (+%11). 2026 beklentisi yükseltildi: düzeltilmiş faaliyet kârı büyümesi yaklaşık %12 (önce %9), düzeltilmiş hisse başına kâr büyümesi yaklaşık %10 (önce %7). 30 Eylül 2026'da özsermaye 554,4 milyon dolar. İlk yarıda (8 Eylül 2026 ara raporu) kâr 107,0 milyon dolar, seyreltilmiş hisse başına kâr 1,58 dolardı (2,71); geçen yılın ilk yarısında Multifonds satışından 136,5 milyon dolarlık kazanç vardı.
risks: Özsermaye geri alım ve temettüyle küçültüldü; yüksek özsermaye kârlılığı kısmen bundan gelir. Borç 842,2 milyon dolar, nakit 150,8 milyon dolar (30 Haziran 2026); kaynağa göre net borç/FAVÖK 2,5.
Hisse bazlı ücret dönem kârının %23'ü kadardır (ilk yarı 2026). Şirketin açıkladığı düzeltilmiş kâr ve beklentiler bu gideri saymaz.
Tek müşterinin ayrılması 2026 büyümesini belirgin düşürdü; büyük sözleşmelerin zamanlaması çeyrek sonuçlarını oynatır.
Şirket dolar ile raporlar, gelirini birçok ülkeden kazanır; enflasyon düzeltmesi İsviçre enflasyonuyla yapılmıştır. Kur, frank cinsinden kârı ve oranları değiştirir.
Maddi olmayan varlıklar (1.259,9 milyon dolar) özsermayenin üç katından fazladır; additiv alımı bunu artırdı. Değer düşüklüğü özsermayeyi hızla eritir.

en.one: Sells core banking software to banks; most revenue recurs. Narrow moat. Buybacks have shrunk equity, so the return ratio looks higher than it is.
en.business: Temenos sells core banking software to banks: the system that runs accounts, loans and payments. It earns subscription and cloud (SaaS) fees, maintenance contracts and implementation services. In 2025 revenue was 1,090.8 million dollars and operating profit 248.0 million dollars. In the third quarter of 2026, 121.8 million dollars of revenue was subscription and SaaS, 134.7 million maintenance and 36.2 million services. Annual recurring revenue (ARR) is 903.6 million dollars. The company reports in US dollars; the share trades in Swiss francs.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. Evidence: a core banking system carries all of a bank's transactions; replacing it is a risky project that takes years. So revenue recurs: ARR is 903.6 million dollars, about 79% of the last 12 months' revenue (1,141.6 million dollars). ARR grew 11% in a year. Real return on equity averaged 31.3% over five years and was 18.4% in its lowest year. Why not wide: the ratio also reflects equity shrunk by buybacks (equity was 639.0 million dollars at the end of 2024 and 372.0 million in June 2026); return on invested capital is lower (latest reading 20.8%). Customers do leave: the exit of a single buy-now-pay-later client takes 3 points off ARR growth and 5 points off subscription revenue in 2026. A large contract slipping by a few days makes the company miss a quarterly target (third quarter: target at least 30%, actual 22%). We looked for gross margin through the inflation years; it is not in the documents read.
en.mgmt: Profit goes to dividends and buybacks; debt is rising too. In 2025 the company bought 320.4 million dollars of its own shares. In the first half of 2026 it bought 114.2 million dollars (1,244,986 shares for 89.8 million francs, about 72 francs a share) and paid 117.9 million dollars in dividends (1.40 francs per share). The 2026 AGM cancelled 3,952,656 shares. A new buyback of up to 100 million francs started on 13 August 2026; the shares will be held for employee plans and acquisitions. Share-based pay is high: 24.6 million dollars in the first half, 23% of the period's profit (107.0 million dollars). The company's "non-IFRS" profit leaves it out; we do not rely on that measure. Restructuring costs appear every period (first half 2026: 8.0 million dollars; first half 2025: 25.8 million); we treat them as ordinary costs. additiv was acquired on 17 July 2026 (preliminary price 226.7 million francs). Intangible assets are 1,259.9 million dollars, more than three times equity; goodwill is not shown separately. We looked for pension and off-balance-sheet commitments and for the shareholder structure; they are not in the documents read.
en.latest: 27 October 2026: The company published third-quarter results. Revenue was 292.5 million dollars (258.5 a year earlier), operating profit 84.8 million dollars (60.1), net profit 63.4 million dollars (44.4) and diluted earnings per share 0.92 dollars (0.65). ARR was 903.6 million dollars (+11%). The 2026 outlook was raised: adjusted operating profit growth of about 12% (was 9%) and adjusted earnings per share growth of about 10% (was 7%). Equity was 554.4 million dollars at 30 September 2026. In the first half (interim report of 8 September 2026) profit was 107.0 million dollars and diluted earnings per share 1.58 dollars (2.71); the first half of last year included a gain of 136.5 million dollars on the sale of Multifonds.
risks: Equity has been shrunk by buybacks and dividends; the high return on equity partly comes from that. Borrowings are 842.2 million dollars and cash 150.8 million (30 June 2026); net debt to EBITDA is 2.5 according to the source.
Share-based pay equals 23% of the period's profit (first half 2026). The company's adjusted profit and its guidance do not count this cost.
The loss of one client cut 2026 growth noticeably; the timing of large contracts moves quarterly results.
The company reports in US dollars and earns its revenue in many countries; the inflation adjustment uses Swiss inflation. Exchange rates change profit and ratios measured in francs.
Intangible assets (1,259.9 million dollars) are more than three times equity; the additiv purchase added to them. An impairment would erode equity quickly.

verify.tr: Evrendeki PD/DD 16,0, oran sayfasındaki 11,9. Fark üç şeyden geliyor. (1) Farklı bilanço: şirketin tablolarına göre özsermaye 30 Haziran 2026'da 372,0 milyon dolar (31 Aralık 2025: 478,0). Üçüncü çeyrek tablolarında 30 Eylül 2026 özsermayesi 554,4 milyon dolar. Oran sayfası (27 Ekim 2026) eylül bilançosunu kullanıyor: 5.373,8 milyon frank ÷ 11,88 = 452 milyon frank, yani 554,4 milyon doların dolar başına yaklaşık 0,82 frankla karşılığı. Evren haziran bilançosuna dayanıyor. (2) Geri alım ve temettü: ilk yarıda 114,2 milyon dolarlık pay alındı ve 117,9 milyon dolar temettü ödendi; özsermaye altı ayda 106 milyon dolar düştü. (3) Para birimi: özsermaye dolar, piyasa değeri frank. Şirketin kendi kur varsayımıyla (dolar başına 0,80 frank) haziran özsermayesi 297,6 milyon frank eder; PD/DD 18,1 çıkar. Evrendeki 16,0 bununla tam tutmuyor (335,7 milyon frank özsermaye ima ediyor); kaynağın kullandığı kur ya da pay sayısı farklı olabilir. Eylülde özsermayenin 182 milyon dolar artmasının nedeni okunamadı: 17 Temmuz 2026'da tamamlanan additiv alımının ön bedeli 226,7 milyon frank, ödenen nakit 135,3 milyon dolar; kalanın payla ödenmiş olması olasıdır ama belgede görülmedi. Eylül rakamı şirket bülteninin ikincil bir kopyasından okundu.
verify.en: P/B is 16.0 in the universe and 11.9 on the ratio page. Three things explain the gap. (1) Different balance sheets: the company's statements show equity of 372.0 million dollars at 30 June 2026 (31 December 2025: 478.0). The third-quarter statements show equity of 554.4 million dollars at 30 September 2026. The ratio page (27 October 2026) uses the September balance sheet: 5,373.8 million francs ÷ 11.88 = 452 million francs, which is 554.4 million dollars at about 0.82 francs per dollar. The universe rests on the June balance sheet. (2) Buybacks and dividends: in the first half the company bought 114.2 million dollars of shares and paid 117.9 million dollars in dividends; equity fell by 106 million dollars in six months. (3) Currency: equity is in dollars, market value in francs. At the company's own planning rate (0.80 francs per dollar) June equity is 297.6 million francs and P/B is 18.1. The universe's 16.0 does not match this exactly (it implies equity of 335.7 million francs); the source may use a different rate or share count. Why equity rose by 182 million dollars by September could not be read: the additiv acquisition completed on 17 July 2026 had a preliminary price of 226.7 million francs and the cash paid was 135.3 million dollars; the rest may have been paid in shares, but this was not seen in a document. The September figure was read in a secondary copy of the company release.

basis.tr: Hesap son 12 ayın kârına dayanır. Şirket hisse başına kâr beklentisi açıklamıyor; son 12 ayda tek seferlik sayılacak önemli bir kazanç bulunmadı. Kazanç olduğu gibi alındı.
basis.en: The calculation rests on the profit of the last 12 months. The company gives no earnings-per-share outlook, and no material one-off gain was found in the last 12 months. Earnings were taken as they are.

basis.tr: Formül yılda %10,8 büyüme veriyordu. En güncel veriler (hisse başına kâr, yıllık değişim): Temmuz-Eylül 2026 çeyreği %41,5. İlk yarı karşılaştırması kullanılmadı: geçen yılın ilk yarısındaki kârın içinde Multifonds satışından 136,5 milyon dolarlık tek seferlik kazanç vardı (hisse başına kâr 2,71 dolardan 1,58 dolara indi). En düşüğü, enflasyondan arındırılınca, %39,4. Bu, formülün hızının yarısından az değil; hız indirilmedi.
basis.en: The formula gave growth of 10.8% a year. Latest figures (earnings per share, year on year): July-September 2026 quarter 41.5%. The first-half comparison was not used: last year's first-half profit included a one-off gain of 136.5 million dollars on the sale of Multifonds (earnings per share went from 2.71 dollars to 1.58). The lowest, after inflation, is 39.4%. That is not less than half the formula's rate; the rate was not lowered.

en.one: Maker of electrical distribution equipment, motors and automation. Narrow moat, low debt. Orders are at a record on data-centre demand; earnings depend on the cycle.
en.business: ABB works in three business areas: Electrification (switchgear, panels, distribution equipment), Motion (motors and drives) and Automation. In 2025 revenue was 33,220 million dollars and income from operations 6,047 million dollars. In the first half of 2026 Electrification had revenue of 9,813 million dollars and an operational EBITA margin of 24.5%, Motion 4,359 million and 18.5%, Automation 4,340 million and 15.0%. The Robotics arm is being sold to SoftBank and is shown as a discontinued operation. The company reports in US dollars.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. Evidence: operational EBITA margin was 19.0% in 2025 and 21.4% in the first nine months of 2026; company-reported return on capital employed (ROCE) is 29.9%. Gross margin was 40.0% in the first nine months of 2026 (41.3% a year earlier). Real return on equity averaged 25.3% over five years and was 14.8% in its lowest year. The edge comes from the installed base, the brand and the breadth of the range; a customer does not easily replace a proven supplier of critical electrical equipment. Why not wide: margins differ a lot across the three areas (Automation 15.0%); large rivals such as Siemens, Schneider and Eaton serve the same markets; and today's high margin partly rests on the data-centre and electrification investment wave. Gross margin fell 1.3 points this year. We looked for gross margin in 2022, when inflation rose; it is not in the documents read.
en.mgmt: Information on a controlling shareholder is not in the documents read. Profit goes to dividends and buybacks: a dividend of 0.94 francs per share for 2025; a buyback of up to 2 billion dollars started on 9 February 2026 (147 million dollars in the second quarter); 20,744,831 shares were cancelled in April 2026. The average buyback price is not in the documents. Net debt was 2,320 million dollars at 30 June 2026, 0.3 times EBITDA. The portfolio is changing: Robotics is being sold to SoftBank at an enterprise value of 5.375 billion dollars (expected net cash about 4.8 billion); the money will buy Rotork for about 5.5 billion dollars (closing in the first half of 2027). About 495 million dollars will be paid for 51% of Mitsubishi Electric's low-voltage business. Both purchases are close to the core business. The E-mobility arm loses money (2025: 148 million dollars; first half of 2026: 65 million). Restructuring costs appear every year (about 200 million dollars expected for 2026); we treat them as ordinary costs. Net pension assets were 511 million dollars (end of 2025). We looked for share-based pay and goodwill; they are not in the documents read.
en.latest: 20 October 2026: The company published third-quarter results. Orders were 12,055 million dollars (+40%), revenue 9,701 million dollars (+14%), income from operations 1,846 million dollars (+15%) and operational EBITA margin 20.8%. Net income attributable to ABB was 1,181 million dollars (−2%) and earnings per share 0.65 dollars (0.66). The fall came from finance costs: a non-cash revaluation of a currency hedge tied to the Rotork acquisition. Over nine months earnings per share were 2.06 dollars (1.89; +9%) and free cash flow 3,707 million dollars. For 2026 the company expects comparable revenue growth in the low teens and a rise of at least 2.7 points in operational EBITA margin. A real estate gain of about 240 million francs will be booked in the fourth quarter.
risks: Profit includes gains on real estate sales: 377 million dollars in the first quarter of 2026 and about 140 million dollars in 2025; about 240 million francs more will come in the fourth quarter. These are not ordinary earnings of the business.

Order growth rests on data-centre and electrification investment (data-centre orders rose by a triple-digit rate in the third quarter). If that wave slows, orders and margins fall; five years of history do not show a full cycle.
The Rotork acquisition (about 5.5 billion dollars) and the Robotics sale are not yet completed; if approvals are delayed or the sale fails, the capital plan changes.
The company reports in US dollars and earns its revenue all over the world; the inflation adjustment uses Swiss inflation.
Provisions are being booked for legacy claims (about 100 million dollars in the second quarter of 2026); more may follow.

en.one: A leading maker of fragrances and flavours; formulas developed with customers make the moat wide. First-half 2026 profit fell on litigation provisions and debt rose.
en.business: Givaudan makes fragrances for perfumes, detergents and personal care products, and flavours and taste solutions for food and drink. Its customers are consumer goods companies. In 2025 sales were 7,472 million francs, EBITDA 1,751 million francs (23.4%) and net income 1,071 million francs. In the first half of 2026 Fragrance & Beauty had sales of 2,010 million francs and Taste & Wellbeing 1,789 million francs.
en.moat_text: The moat is wide. Evidence: gross margin was 44.1% in 2024, 43.5% in 2025 and 44.5% in the first half of 2026; input costs rose in 2026, the company says price increases fully offset them, and gross margin went up. A fragrance or flavour is the identity of the customer's product but a small part of its cost; the formula is developed with the customer, and changing it means changing how the product tastes or smells. Real return on equity averaged 21.0% over five years and was 17.6% in its lowest year: all five readings are close together. The weak side: Taste & Wellbeing sales fell 6.3% in the first half and its margin slipped (EBITDA margin 18.3%; 22.0% a year earlier) while growth leaned on fine fragrance. Competition authorities in several countries are investigating the fragrance industry; in the first half the company booked a provision for a related agreement.
en.mgmt: The shareholder structure is not in the documents read. Most profit goes to dividends: 72.00 francs per share for 2025 (664 million francs paid in the first half of 2026); the payout ratio is 69.6% according to the source. There is no buyback (looked for, not in the documents). Debt is high: net debt was 4,604 million francs at 30 June 2026, 2.8 times EBITDA (end of 2025: 3,678 million francs and 2.1). Acquisitions continue: Belle Aire Creations was bought on 1 December 2025 for 188 million francs and 51% of Vollmens on 1 September 2025 for 34 million francs; an agreement for a majority stake in Eurofragance was announced on 5 June 2026 (price not disclosed). All are within the core business. Intangible assets are 4,687 million francs, more than equity attributable to the parent (4,402 million francs); total goodwill is not shown separately. Share-based pay was 40 million francs in the first half, 8.4% of net income (27 million a year earlier). "One-off" costs appear every year: 51 million francs in 2024, 56 million in 2025 and 103 million in the first half of 2026; that is why we treat the company's adjusted profit with caution. Pension liabilities are 152 million francs.
en.latest: 13 October 2026: The company published nine-month sales: 5.89 billion francs (5.74 a year earlier; +2.6%). Third-quarter sales were 2.09 billion francs (+11%; like-for-like +8.6%); Fragrance & Beauty 1.14 billion francs (+18%) and Taste & Wellbeing 952 million francs (+4.5%). First-half results (approved by the board on 21 July 2026): sales 3,799 million francs (−1.7%; like-for-like +3.6%), EBITDA 820 million francs (−13.3%), net income 475 million francs (−19.8%) and earnings per share 51.46 francs (64.18). Most of the fall comes from one-off costs of 103 million francs, of which 83 million are litigation settlements and provisions (the competition investigation and a diacetyl case in the United States). Adjusted earnings per share were 60.25 francs (66.71; −9.7%).
risks: Debt is close to the threshold: net debt is 2.8 times EBITDA (company figure) and 2.9 according to the source; the limit is 3. A new acquisition or a fall in EBITDA would eliminate the company at wall 2.

The competition authorities' investigation of the fragrance industry continues (Europe, the United States, the United Kingdom, Switzerland and other countries); the company says it cannot estimate the financial impact. Diacetyl lawsuits and lawsuits over the 2024 Louisville explosion are also open.
Adjusted profit fell too (−9.7% in the first half) and the Taste & Wellbeing margin dropped; this may not be temporary.
Share-based pay equals 8.4% of net income and rose from 27 million to 40 million francs in a year.
Most sales are outside Switzerland; a stronger franc lowers sales and profit in francs. The inflation adjustment uses Swiss inflation.

SCHN.business: Schindler asansör ve yürüyen merdiven üretir, kurar, sonra yıllarca bakımını ve yenilemesini yapar. en.one: Installs and maintains elevators and escalators. Narrow moat, net cash balance sheet, family controlled. Margin is rising after a four-year recovery.
en.business: Schindler makes and installs elevators and escalators, then maintains and modernises them for years. It has three lines: new installations, modernisation and service. In 2025 revenue was 10,947 million francs, operating profit 1,384 million francs (12.6%) and net profit 1,073 million francs (1,015 million attributable to shareholders). The revenue shares of the lines are not in the documents read.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. Evidence: every installed elevator brings years of maintenance income; the company says service markets grew healthily in 2025 and modernisation expanded steadily with an ageing installed base. Operating margin was 12.6% in 2025 and 13.5% in the first nine months of 2026. Return on invested capital is very high according to the source (latest reading 51.6%), because the business needs little capital and customers pay in advance. Real return on equity averaged 18.6% over five years. Why not wide: in its lowest year (2022) real return on equity fell to 11.7%; when costs rose, prices did not follow at once and the company had to run a four-year recovery plan. New installations depend on construction and are won by tender; the company says high construction costs weighed on new installations in 2025, and in 2026 every region except China grew. We looked for the renewal rate of service contracts and the share of service revenue; they are not in the documents read.
en.mgmt: The company is family controlled: the Schindler and Bonnard families hold 68.6% of voting rights under shareholder agreements (31 December 2025). There are two classes: registered shares with votes (67,077,452) and participation certificates without votes (40,716,831). Profit returns to the owners: an ordinary dividend of 6.00 francs and an extraordinary dividend of 0.80 francs per share for 2025 (733 million francs in total; 72% of profit attributable to shareholders). Between 6 November 2024 and 5 November 2026 about 653 million francs of shares and certificates were bought back (703,995 shares and 1,739,751 certificates); they will be cancelled. The average purchase price was not disclosed. The balance sheet is in net cash (net debt to EBITDA −1.4 according to the source). Share-based pay is small: certificates worth 18 million francs were allocated in 2025 (1.8% of profit attributable to shareholders). Related-party transactions are small (revenue of 8 million francs from associates). Restructuring costs continue: the adjusted margin is 0.3 to 0.7 points above the reported margin (2025: 13.3% and 12.6%); we treat them as ordinary costs. We looked for goodwill, pension obligations and acquisitions; they are not in the sections read.
en.latest: 22 October 2026: The company published nine-month results. Orders were 8,735 million francs (+5.2% in local currencies), revenue 8,162 million francs (+2.6%), operating profit 1,102 million francs, operating margin 13.5%, net profit 852 million francs (+7.0%) and operating cash flow 903 million francs. Third-quarter orders rose 10.3% in local currencies. The 2026 operating margin outlook was raised from about 13% to about 13.5%. In the first half (21 July 2026) net profit attributable to shareholders was 514 million francs (502) and earnings per share 4.82 francs (4.67). On 6 November 2026 the company announced that the buyback programme was completed.
risks: New installations depend on the construction cycle; revenue in China fell in 2026. In 2022 rising costs cut real return on equity to 11.7%; that is why the five-year record is not steady.
Part of the margin gain comes from efficiency programmes; it is unclear whether the gain continues once they end.
The family holds 68.6% of the votes; minority shareholders have limited influence and participation certificates carry no vote.

Most revenue is outside Switzerland; a stronger franc lowers revenue in francs (in the first half of 2026 revenue fell 2.9% in francs while rising in local currencies). The inflation adjustment uses Swiss inflation.
watch: Operating margin (2026 outlook about 13.5%)
Order intake, especially new installations and China
Growth in service and modernisation
Cancellation of repurchased shares and any new programme

KNIN.moat_text: Hendek zayıf sınıfta; şirket bu yüzden 3. suru geçemedi. Üstünlük ölçekten gelir: büyük hacim taşıyıcıdan iyi fiyat ve yer almayı sağlar, iş az sermaye ister ve reel özsermaye kârlılığı yüksektir (beş yılda ortalama %49,1, en düşük %33,6). KNIN.mgmt: Ortaklık yapısı, temettü ve geri alım bu çalıştırmada şirketin kendi belgesinden okunamadı (şirket sitesi açılamadı); kaynağa göre dağıtım oranı %73, temettü verimi %2,5. Şirket maliyet programı yürütüyor: 2026'da 150 milyon frankın üstünde brüt tasarruf bekleniyor. Sözleşmeli lojistik kolunun 2026'nın ilk çeyreğindeki kârında bir sat ve geri kirala işleminden tek seferlik kazanç var (dokuz aylık faaliyet kârı 211 milyon frank, düzeltilmiş 176 milyon frank). en.one: A large global sea and air freight forwarder. It has scale, but profit swings with freight rates; the moat did not meet our test.
en.business: Kuehne+Nagel moves freight without owning ships or aircraft: it buys space from carriers for the customer's cargo and arranges customs and storage. It has four lines: sea freight, air freight, road transport and contract logistics (warehousing). In the third quarter of 2026 net turnover was 7,386 million francs and operating profit 435 million francs; 172 million francs of that came from sea, 169 million from air, 28 million from road and 66 million from contract logistics.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak; this is why the company did not pass wall 3. The edge comes from scale: large volumes buy better prices and space from carriers, the business needs little capital and real return on equity is high (five-year average 49.1%, lowest 33.6%). But the edge does not turn into pricing power: profit moves quickly with freight rates and volumes. Real return on equity was 74.0% in 2021 and 33.7% in 2025; according to the source, real profit shrank by about 23% a year over five years. Even within a year the swings are large: in the third quarter of 2026 operating profit rose 53% and air freight profit went from 92 million to 169 million francs, while nine-month gross profit in sea freight fell from 1,612 million to 1,463 million francs. Customers award cargo by tender and under short contracts, and changing forwarder is easy. This is close to what our principles call "work won by bid"; because of the scale we gave 1 rather than 0.
en.mgmt: The shareholder structure, dividends and buybacks could not be read from the company's own documents in this run (the company site could not be opened); according to the source the payout ratio is 73% and the dividend yield 2.5%. The company is running a cost programme: gross savings of more than 150 million francs are expected in 2026. The contract logistics result for the first quarter of 2026 includes a one-off gain on a sale-and-leaseback (nine-month operating profit 211 million francs, adjusted 176 million). A long-term partnership with Amazon and a compensation instrument tied to milestones over up to seven years were announced; the details could not be read. Share-based pay, goodwill, pensions and off-balance-sheet commitments could not be checked. Because of these gaps the D and E scores were set cautiously.
en.latest: 22 October 2026: The company published third-quarter results. Net turnover was 7.39 billion francs (+22%), gross profit 2.39 billion francs (+13%), operating profit 435 million francs (+53%) and net profit 316 million francs (+53%). Air freight turnover rose 37% excluding currency effects (cloud infrastructure and semiconductor shipments) and volume grew 10%; sea freight volume rose 5%. The 2026 operating profit outlook was raised from 1.35-1.55 billion francs to 1.5-1.6 billion francs.
risks: Profit depends on freight rates and world trade volumes; the exceptional profits of 2021-2022 have not returned and the five-year trend is downward.
Today's rise comes largely from data-centre and semiconductor shipments in air freight; if that demand slows, profit falls quickly.
The company earns its revenue all over the world; the inflation adjustment uses Swiss inflation.
watch: Conversion of gross profit into operating profit (18.2% in the third quarter)
Sea and air freight volumes and unit profit

en.one: Maker of high-performance plastics (polyamides); operating margin above 30% and no debt. The moat is narrow; the five-year real profit trend points down.
en.business: EMS works in two areas: High Performance Polymers (special plastics that replace metal) and Specialty Chemicals. In the first half of 2026 net sales were 1,010 million francs, operating profit 309 million francs (30.6%) and net income 259 million francs. Polymers brought 913 million francs of sales and specialty chemicals 99 million (provisional figures). In 2025 net sales were 1,950 million francs and operating profit 567 million francs. The company names electric cars, robotics and data centres as growth areas.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The evidence is in the margin: operating margin was 29.1% in the first half of 2025 and 30.6% in the first half of 2026; 32.0% in polymers. For a chemicals company this level shows the product is not a commodity but a part developed for the customer. Pricing power shows too: the company says it passed higher raw material and energy costs on to selling prices at once in 2026, and the margin rose while sales in francs fell. Real return on equity averaged 25.0% over five years; the lowest reading is the last 12 months, 20.9%. Why not wide: profitability has come down from 30.1% in 2021 and, according to the source, real profit shrank by about 6% a year over five years; sales were 2,071 million francs in 2024 and 1,950 million in 2025. Demand depends on industrial and automotive production. We looked for the automotive share of sales and customer concentration; they are not in the documents read.
en.mgmt: Almost all profit is paid to shareholders: for 2025/26 an ordinary dividend of 14.65 francs and an extraordinary dividend of 3.75 francs per share, 18.40 francs in total (17.25 a year earlier), paid on 13 August 2026. The payout ratio is 85% according to the source. The balance sheet is very strong: equity of 2,098 million francs and an equity ratio of 81.1% (30 June 2026); the company is in net cash according to the source. Investment needs are low (12 million francs in the first half). The shareholder structure is not in the documents read; Magdalena Martullo is among the board members. We looked for acquisitions, buybacks, share-based pay, goodwill, restructuring costs and pension obligations; they are not in the documents read.
en.latest: 22 October 2026: The company published nine-month net sales: 1.51 billion francs (1.49 a year earlier); +4.2% in local currencies. The 2026 sales outlook was raised to "previous year's level"; operating profit is expected slightly above last year. Definitive first-half results published on 28 August 2026: net sales 1,010 million francs (1,020; +4.3% in local currencies), operating profit 309 million francs (296; +4.4%), net income 259 million francs (253; +2.5%) and operating cash flow 243 million francs (199).
risks: The five-year real profit trend points down; the calculation therefore assumes profit keeps shrinking. In the first half net income rose only 2.5%.
Demand depends on the industrial and automotive production cycle; the company expects a challenging economic environment in the fourth quarter.

Much of production is in Switzerland and most sales are abroad: a strong franc lowers sales in francs (first half: +4.3% in local currencies, −0.9% in francs). The inflation adjustment uses Swiss inflation.
Energy and raw material prices rose with supply shortages in the Middle East; if price increases cannot be passed on, the margin narrows.

en.one: Europe's leader in sanitary technology, with a wide moat built on behind-the-wall systems and plumber loyalty. It passed Wall 3; earnings depend on European construction.
en.business: Geberit sells sanitary products for buildings: concealed cisterns and installation systems, piping systems and bathroom ceramics. Its products reach plumbers through wholesalers. In 2025 net sales were 3,162.9 million francs, EBITDA 930.6 million francs (29.4%) and net income 597.8 million francs. In the first nine months of 2026 net sales were 2,535 million francs with an EBITDA margin of 30.7%.
en.moat_text: The moat is wide. The evidence is in the margins: EBITDA margin was 29.6% in 2024, 29.4% in 2025 and 30.7% in the first nine months of 2026. Real return on equity ranged from 36.6% to 44.7% over five years and averaged 40.3%. Pricing power was tested in 2026: the company says direct material and energy prices rose sharply and currency losses were large; with sales price increases and volume growth, operating margins stayed at last year's level. The product is installed behind the wall and stays there for decades; the plumber returns to the system he knows. Building such an installer network and product range would take a rival years and a lot of capital. The weak side: sales depend on Europe and on construction activity; the company still sees no broad market recovery in Europe. We looked for gross margin in the 2022 inflation year; it is not in the sections read.
en.mgmt: There is no controlling shareholder; the company states a free float of 100% and 49,800 registered shareholders. Almost all profit returns to owners: 503 million francs were distributed in 2025 (422 million in dividends, 81 million in buybacks), 76% of free cash flow. A dividend of 12.90 francs per share was proposed for 2025 (71.1% of net income). In 2025 the company bought back 145,231 shares for 81 million francs; that is about 558 francs a share (our arithmetic), roughly 31 times that year's earnings per share. The buyback was accelerated in the first half of 2026; net debt rose to 1.33 billion francs at the end of June (1.17 billion a year earlier). Goodwill and intangible assets are 1,310.7 million francs, 86% of equity (1,517.1 million francs at the end of 2025). They stem from an old acquisition; there has been no large purchase in recent years. In 2025 the closure of a ceramics plant in Germany cost 18 million euros of one-off charges at EBITDA level. We looked for share-based pay and pension obligations; they are not in the sections read.
en.latest: 3 November 2026: The company reported the first nine months. Net sales were 2,535 million francs (+3.6% in francs; +5.7% currency-adjusted). EBITDA was 778 million francs (+3.3%), a margin of 30.7%. Net income was 529 million francs (+7.1%) and earnings per share 16.23 francs (+8.1%). In the third quarter net sales were 824 million francs and net income 166 million francs (156 million a year earlier). The 2026 outlook was kept: sales growth of 5-6% in local currencies and an EBITDA margin at last year's level. First half, announced on 19 August 2026: net income 364 million francs (339) and earnings per share 11.09 francs (10.28).
risks: Sales depend on construction and renovation activity in Europe; the company still sees no broad recovery there. Five years of history may not show a full construction cycle.
Rising raw material, energy and wage costs squeeze the margin; in 2026 material prices rose sharply and the margin was held only through price increases. Personnel expenses rose 6.2% in 2025.
The company reports in francs while most sales are in other currencies: in the first nine months of 2026 currency effects cut sales by 52 million francs.
Equity is small because of buybacks; goodwill and intangible assets are 86% of equity. Buybacks are made at a high price and raised net debt in 2026.

en.one: World leader in dental implants with a strong brand and no net debt. It passed Wall 3, but profitability has fallen and "one-off" charges recur.
en.business: Straumann sells dental implants, prosthetic parts, clear aligners (ClearCorrect) and digital dentistry equipment; its customers are dentists and dental labs. In 2025 revenue was 2,605 million francs, operating profit 549 million francs (21.1%) and net profit 358 million francs. In the first half of 2026 revenue was 1,379.5 million francs: Europe, Middle East and Africa 573.4; North America 352.4; Asia Pacific 324.8; Latin America 128.9 million francs.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow: real and proven by numbers, but its durability is being tested. Gross margin is high: 71.2% in 2024, 68.6% in 2025 and 72.0% in the first half of 2026 (including tariff refunds; 70.5% on the company's "core" measure). The company says it is gaining share in premium implants; organic growth was 8.9% in 2025 and 7.8% in the first half of 2026. Once a dentist is used to an implant system, the training and instruments are not easily swapped. Why not wide: real return on equity fell from 27.6% in 2021 to 16.9% in 2025 and 15.3% over the last 12 months. In China the state sets the price: a second round of volume-based procurement is awaited, with implementation expected in early 2027. Operating margin fell from 24.0% in 2024 to 21.1% in 2025. In clear aligners the company is not the leader and is in litigation with Align. We looked for a market share figure; it is not in the documents read.
en.mgmt: There is net cash: 34.7 million francs at 30 June 2026; equity is 58.6% of assets. About a third of profit goes to dividends (1.00 franc per share for 2025); the rest stays in the company and goes into investment: capital expenditure rose 33% to 223.5 million francs in 2025 (Shanghai campus, Neodent plant in Brazil). The return on retained profit is not visible yet: earnings per share were 2.87 francs in 2024 and 2.24 francs in 2025 (continuing operations). "One-off" charges recur: litigation costs of 25 million in 2024, 28 million in 2025 and 18.0 million francs in the first half of 2026; restructuring costs of 53.2 million francs in 2025. That is why we do not rely on the company's "core" profit. Share-based pay was 18.9 million francs in 2025 (5.3% of net profit). Buybacks are small: 24.6 million francs in 2025. Intangible assets (including goodwill) are 872.2 million francs, 40% of equity (2,164.7 million francs). Pension obligations are 43.6 million francs. Management is changing: Guillaume Daniellot is leaving after seven years as CEO. We looked for the shareholder structure; it is not in the sections read.
en.latest: 19 August 2026: The company reported first-half results. Revenue was 1,379.5 million francs (+2.3% in francs; +7.8% organic). Operating profit was 350.6 million francs (329.6), net profit 250.7 million francs (238.2) and earnings per share 1.57 francs (1.49). On the company's "core" measure net profit was 262.0 million francs (265.7) and earnings per share 1.64 francs (1.66). Profit includes 21.6 million francs of one-off income (mostly tariff refunds) and 18.0 million francs of Align litigation costs. Free cash flow was 168.6 million francs (113.0). The 2026 outlook: high single-digit organic growth and a rise of 140-170 basis points in core operating margin at constant exchange rates. In the third quarter revenue was 667.1 million francs with organic growth of 9.2%; China returned to growth.
risks: In China the state's volume-based procurement sets implant prices; the second round is expected to take effect in early 2027. If prices fall again, Asia Pacific profit falls.
Profitability is declining: real return on equity fell from 27.6% to 16.9% in five years. The company retains about two thirds of its profit, yet earnings per share fell from 2024 to 2025.
Litigation and restructuring charges have recurred for three years (81 million francs in total in 2025); the company's "core" profit leaves them out. Share-based pay is 5.3% of net profit.
Implants and aligners are paid for by the patient; when consumer confidence weakens, demand is postponed. The company says demand in North America is cautious.
The company reports in francs while most sales are in other currencies: in the first half of 2026 organic growth was 7.8% but growth in francs only 2.3%. Tariffs affect gross margin.

PGHN.one: Özel piyasalarda 186 milyar dolar yöneten varlık yöneticisi. 3. suru geçti; ama son 12 ayın kârı yüksek performans ücreti içeriyor, fonlardan çıkış talebi arttı.
PGHN.business: Partners Group, müşterilerinin parasını özel sermaye, özel kredi, altyapı ve gayrimenkule yatırır. İki geliri var: yönetilen varlık üzerinden yönetim ücreti ve yatırımlar kârla satılınca performans ücreti. 30 Haziran 2026'da yönetilen varlık 186 milyar dolar. 2025'te gelir 2.563 milyon frank (yönetim 1.744, performans 819), FAVÖK 1.611 milyon frank, kâr 1.261 milyon frank. 2026'nın ilk yarısında gelir 1.121 milyon frank; performans ücretinin payı %19 (geçen yıl %29).
PGHN.moat_text: Hendek dar sınıfta. Kanıt: FAVÖK marjı 2026'nın ilk yarısında %63,0 (geçen yıl %64,0); yönetim geliri sabit kurla %12 arttı; ilk yarıda 16 milyar dolarlık rekor yeni taahhüt toplandı. Müşteri parası uzun vadeli programlara ve kişiye özel çözümlere bağlıdır; bu ölçeği ve yatırım geçmişini kurmak yıllar ister. Reel özsermaye kârlılığı beş yılda ortalama %50,1, en düşük yılında %34,1; şirketin kendi belgesine göre aktif kârlılığı 2025'te %19,7 (kâr 1.261 ÷ aktif 6.388 milyon frank). Neden geniş değil: yönetilen varlığın yaklaşık %30'u istenince çıkılabilen ("evergreen") fonlardadır ve bu para kaçabiliyor. 2026'nın ilk yarısında bu fonlara 4,2 milyar dolar girdi, 3,8 milyar dolar çıktı; şirket haziran başında yaklaşık 8,6 milyar dolarlık bir fonda çıkışları sınırladı ve üç olgun stratejiden orta vadede 10-20 milyar dolar net çıkışı olası görüyor. Gelirin yönetilen varlığa oranı %1,75'ten %1,54'e indi.
PGHN.mgmt: Kârın neredeyse tamamı temettüye gidiyor: 2025 için hisse başına 46,00 frank önerildi (seyreltilmiş hisse başına kâr 48,45 frank). 2025'te 333,6 milyon franklık kendi payı alındı; bunlar çalışan pay planlarında kullanılıyor. Hisse bazlı ücret 2025'te 62,6 milyon frank (kârın %5,0'ı). Kusur: temettü ve müşterilerle birlikte yapılan yatırımlar borçla besleniyor. 2025 sonunda tahvil borcu 1.330 milyon frank, kullanılan kredi 1.056 milyon frank (2024: 715), nakit 328,8 milyon frank; özsermaye 2.414 milyondan 2.187 milyon franka, özsermayenin aktife oranı %42'den %34'e indi. Şirketin kendi yatırımları 1.677 milyon frank; çağrılmamış taahhütleri 359,9 milyon frank. Maddi olmayan varlıklar ve şerefiye 364,9 milyon frank (özsermayenin %17'si). Yönetim değişiyor: 1 Ocak 2027'den itibaren Roberto Cagnati ve Juri Jenkner eş CEO olacak; David Layton yatırım komitesinin başına geçiyor (FINMA onayına bağlı). Kurucuların payına bakıldı; okunan bölümlerde yok.
PGHN.latest: 1 Eylül 2026: Şirket ilk yarı sonuçlarını açıkladı. Gelir 1.121 milyon frank (−%7; sabit kurla −%2). Yönetim geliri 905 milyon frank (+%6; sabit kurla +%12), performans geliri 216 milyon frank (−%39). FAVÖK 706 milyon frank (−%9), kâr 502 milyon frank (−%13; sabit kurla aynı düzeyde). Şirkete göre performans geliri düştü, çünkü bazı büyük satışlar 2025'in ikinci yarısına öne çekilmişti. 2026 için performans gelirinin toplam gelirin %20-25'i olması bekleniyor; orta ve uzun vadeli aralık %25-40. 2026 için 26-32 milyar dolar yeni müşteri talebi bekleniyor.
risks: Son 12 ayın kârı yüksek performans ücreti içeriyor: bu dönemde performans ücreti 680 milyon frank, gelirin yaklaşık %27'si; şirket 2026 için %20-25 bekliyor. Performans ücreti satışların zamanına bağlıdır ve yıldan yıla oynar.

İstenince çıkılabilen fonlar yönetilen varlığın yaklaşık %30'u. Çıkış talepleri arttı, bir fonda çıkışlar sınırlandı; şirket üç olgun stratejiden 10-20 milyar dolar net çıkışı olası görüyor. Güven sarsılırsa yönetim ücreti de düşer.
Şirket frankla raporlar, gelirinin çoğu dolar ve avrodur: 2026'nın ilk yarısında kâr sabit kurla aynı kaldı, frank olarak %13 düştü.

Bilanço ağırlaştı: borç ve kullanılan kredi toplamı yaklaşık 2,4 milyar frank, özsermayenin aktife oranı %34. Kendi yatırımlarının değeri piyasayla birlikte düşebilir; ilk yarıda bu yatırımlardan 20 milyon frank zarar yazıldı.
Yönetim değişikliği ve yüksek değerlemeler: şirket yeni özel sermaye alımlarında seçici davrandığını söylüyor; satışlar gecikirse performans ücreti 2027'ye kayar.

en.one: A private markets asset manager with 186 billion dollars. It passed Wall 3, but last-12-month profit includes high performance fees and redemption requests have risen.
en.business: Partners Group invests its clients' money in private equity, private credit, infrastructure and real estate. It has two revenue streams: management fees on assets under management and performance fees when investments are sold at a profit. Assets under management were 186 billion dollars at 30 June 2026. In 2025 revenue was 2,563 million francs (management 1,744, performance 819), EBITDA 1,611 million francs and profit 1,261 million francs. In the first half of 2026 revenue was 1,121 million francs; performance fees were 19% of it (29% a year earlier).
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. Evidence: the EBITDA margin was 63.0% in the first half of 2026 (64.0% a year earlier); management income rose 12% at constant currency; a record 16 billion dollars of new commitments came in during the first half. Client money sits in long-dated programmes and bespoke solutions; building this scale and track record takes years. Real return on equity averaged 50.1% over five years and was 34.1% in its lowest year; from the company's own report, return on assets was 19.7% in 2025 (profit 1,261 ÷ assets 6,388 million francs). Why not wide: about 30% of assets are in evergreen funds that clients can leave on request, and that money can go. In the first half of 2026 these funds took in 4.2 billion dollars and paid out 3.8 billion; in early June the company limited redemptions in a fund of about 8.6 billion dollars, and it sees net outflows of 10-20 billion dollars from three mature strategies as possible in the medium term. Revenue as a share of assets fell from 1.75% to 1.54%.
en.mgmt: Almost all profit goes to dividends: 46.00 francs per share was proposed for 2025 (diluted earnings per share 48.45 francs). In 2025 the company bought 333.6 million francs of its own shares; they are used for employee share plans. Share-based pay was 62.6 million francs in 2025 (5.0% of profit). The flaw: dividends and investments alongside clients are fed by debt. At the end of 2025 bonds outstanding were 1,330 million francs, drawn credit 1,056 million francs (2024: 715) and cash 328.8 million francs; equity fell from 2,414 million to 2,187 million francs and the equity ratio from 42% to 34%. The company's own investments are 1,677 million francs; its uncalled commitments are 359.9 million francs. Intangible assets and goodwill are 364.9 million francs (17% of equity). Management is changing: from 1 January 2027 Roberto Cagnati and Juri Jenkner become co-CEOs and David Layton moves to head the investment committee (subject to FINMA approval). We looked for the founders' stakes; they are not in the sections read.
en.latest: 1 September 2026: The company reported first-half results. Revenue was 1,121 million francs (−7%; −2% at constant currency). Management income was 905 million francs (+6%; +12% at constant currency) and performance income 216 million francs (−39%). EBITDA was 706 million francs (−9%) and profit 502 million francs (−13%; flat at constant currency). The company says performance income fell because several sizeable exits had been brought forward into the second half of 2025. For 2026 performance income is expected to be 20-25% of total revenue; the mid- to long-term range is 25-40%. New client demand of 26-32 billion dollars is expected for 2026.
risks: Last-12-month profit includes high performance fees: 680 million francs in the period, about 27% of revenue; the company expects 20-25% for 2026. Performance fees depend on the timing of exits and swing from year to year.

Evergreen funds are about 30% of assets. Redemption requests have risen and one fund has limited withdrawals; the company sees net outflows of 10-20 billion dollars from three mature strategies as possible. If trust is shaken, management fees fall too.
The company reports in francs while most of its revenue is in dollars and euros: in the first half of 2026 profit was flat at constant currency but fell 13% in francs.

The balance sheet has become heavier: bonds and drawn credit total about 2.4 billion francs and the equity ratio is 34%. The value of its own investments can fall with markets; they produced a loss of 20 million francs in the first half.
Management change and high valuations: the company says it is selective on new private equity deals; if exits are delayed, performance fees slip into 2027.
watch: Inflows and redemptions in evergreen funds (first half 2026: 4.2 and 3.8 billion dollars)

SOON.one: Dünyanın büyük işitme cihazı üreticilerinden; marjı yüksek, talebi istikrarlı. 3. suru geçti; ama tüketici kulaklığı yatırımı zararla kapanıyor.
SOON.business: Sonova işitme cihazları (Phonak) üretir, kendi mağazalarında işitme hizmeti verir ve koklear implant satar. Mali yılı mart sonunda biter. Mart 2026'da biten yılda süren faaliyetlerin satışı 3.605,9 milyon frank, faaliyet kârı 675,8 milyon frank oldu. Eylül 2026'da biten ilk yarıda satış 1.834,1 milyon frank: işitme cihazları kolu 1.716,7, koklear implant 117,4 milyon frank. Tüketici kulaklığı kolu satışa çıkarıldı ve durdurulan faaliyet olarak gösteriliyor.
SOON.moat_text: Hendek dar sınıfta: gerçek ve rakamla kanıtlı. Brüt marj Eylül 2026'da biten ilk yarıda %74,4 (bir yıl önce %72,2); şirketin "çekirdek" faaliyet kâr marjı %20,9 (%18,4). Reel özsermaye kârlılığı beş yılda %18,7 ile %26,1 arasında, ortalama %22,7. Şirket pazarın üstünde büyüdüğünü söylüyor: mart 2026'da biten yılda toptan satış yerel para birimleriyle %9,5 arttı (pazar büyümesi varsayımı %2-4). Kendi çipini ve platformunu geliştirmek (yeni EON platformu) ve kendi mağaza ağını kurmak bir rakip için yıllar ister. Neden geniş değil: pazar payı her yeni platformla el değiştirir; ABD'de gaziler kurumu (VA) ve Costco gibi büyük alıcılar düşük fiyat ister. Koklear implant kolu zayıf: ilk yarıda satış %11,2 düştü, kolun çekirdek faaliyet kârı 7,1 milyon franka indi. Pazar payı rakamına ve 2022 enflasyon yılının brüt marjına bakıldı; okunan belgelerde yok.
SOON.mgmt: Mart 2026'da biten yıl için hisse başına 4,70 frank temettü önerildi (kârın yaklaşık %45'i). Şirket bu mali yılda geri alım öngörmüyor; nedeni olarak satın alma fırsatlarını gösteriyor. Sermaye tahsisinde kusur var: tüketici kulaklığı kolu değer yok etti. Kolun vergi sonrası zararı mart 2026'da biten yılda 106,5 milyon frank, eylül 2026'da biten ilk yarıda 56,8 milyon frank (68,3 milyon franklık değer düşüklüğü dahil). "Tek seferlik" giderler yineleniyor: yeniden yapılanma gideri 2024/25'te 43,9 milyon, 2025/26'da 17,2 milyon, 2026/27'nin ilk yarısında 6,7 milyon frank; ayrıca 2025/26'da 34,7 milyon franklık yazılım değer düşüklüğü, 28,2 milyon franklık dava gideri ve eski bir koklear implant ürünü için 23,6 milyon franklık karşılık. Bu yüzden şirketin "çekirdek" kârına güvenmiyoruz. Net borç 30 Eylül 2026'da 1.072,4 milyon frank (FAVÖK'ün 1,1 katı); özsermaye 2.808,9 milyon frank, aktifin %47,4'ü. Şerefiye tutarına, hisse bazlı ücrete, emeklilik yükümlülüğüne ve ortaklık yapısına bakıldı; okunan belgelerde yok.
SOON.latest: 12 Kasım 2026: Şirket eylül 2026'da biten ilk yarının sonuçlarını açıkladı. Satış 1.834,1 milyon frank (+%6,7; yerel para birimleriyle +%7,5). Faaliyet kârı 372,0 milyon frank (279,9; +%32,9). Hisse başına kâr, durdurulan faaliyetler dahil, 4,22 frank (3,16); süren faaliyetlerde 5,18 frank (3,46). Geçen yılın ilk yarısında 28,2 milyon franklık dava gideri vardı. Faaliyetlerden serbest nakit akışı 287,0 milyon frank (89,7). Yıllık beklenti yükseltildi: yerel para birimleriyle satış büyümesi %6-8 (önce %5-8), çekirdek faaliyet kârı büyümesi %10-13 (önce %7-10).
risks: Tüketici kulaklığı kolunun satışı henüz tamamlanmadı; alıcı ve fiyat açıklanmadı. Satış tamamlanana kadar yeni zarar yazılabilir (ilk yarıda vergi sonrası 56,8 milyon frank).

Pazar payı ürün döngüsüne bağlıdır: yeni EON platformu beklentiyi karşılamazsa ya da rakipler daha iyi bir ürün çıkarırsa büyüme pazarın altına iner. ABD'de büyük alıcılar (VA, Costco) fiyatı aşağı çeker.

Şirket satın almayla büyüyor ve geri alımı bu yüzden durdurdu; net borç 1.072,4 milyon frank. Şerefiye tutarını okuyamadık; pahalı alımlar sermayenin getirisini düşürür.

en.one: A leading hearing aid maker with high margins and steady demand. It passed Wall 3, but its consumer headphone investment is ending in losses.
en.business: Sonova makes hearing aids (Phonak), provides hearing care in its own shops and sells cochlear implants. Its fiscal year ends in March. In the year to March 2026 sales from continuing operations were 3,605.9 million francs and operating profit 675.8 million francs. In the first half to September 2026 sales were 1,834.1 million francs: the Hearing Instruments segment 1,716.7 and Cochlear Implants 117.4 million francs. The Consumer Hearing business is up for sale and shown as a discontinued operation.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow: real and proven by numbers. Gross margin was 74.4% in the first half to September 2026 (72.2% a year earlier); the company's "core" operating margin was 20.9% (18.4%). Real return on equity ranged from 18.7% to 26.1% over five years and averaged 22.7%. The company says it is growing faster than the market: wholesale sales rose 9.5% in local currencies in the year to March 2026 (assumed market growth 2-4%). Developing its own chip and platform (the new EON platform) and building its own shop network would take a rival years. Why not wide: market share changes hands with each new platform; in the United States large buyers such as the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) and Costco demand low prices. The cochlear implant segment is weak: first-half sales fell 11.2% and the segment's core operating profit dropped to 7.1 million francs. We looked for a market share figure and for gross margin in the 2022 inflation year; they are not in the documents read.
en.mgmt: A dividend of 4.70 francs per share was proposed for the year to March 2026 (about 45% of profit). The company plans no buyback this fiscal year, citing acquisition opportunities. Capital allocation has a flaw: the Consumer Hearing business destroyed value. Its after-tax loss was 106.5 million francs in the year to March 2026 and 56.8 million francs in the first half to September 2026 (including a 68.3 million franc write-down). "One-off" charges recur: restructuring costs of 43.9 million in 2024/25, 17.2 million in 2025/26 and 6.7 million francs in the first half of 2026/27; in addition, 2025/26 had a 34.7 million franc software impairment, 28.2 million francs of litigation costs and a 23.6 million franc provision for a legacy cochlear implant product. That is why we do not rely on the company's "core" profit. Net debt was 1,072.4 million francs at 30 September 2026 (1.1 times EBITDA); equity was 2,808.9 million francs, 47.4% of assets. We looked for goodwill, share-based pay, pension obligations and the shareholder structure; they are not in the documents read.
en.latest: 12 November 2026: The company reported results for the first half to September 2026. Sales were 1,834.1 million francs (+6.7%; +7.5% in local currencies). Operating profit was 372.0 million francs (279.9; +32.9%). Earnings per share including discontinued operations were 4.22 francs (3.16); from continuing operations 5.18 francs (3.46). Last year's first half included 28.2 million francs of litigation costs. Operating free cash flow was 287.0 million francs (89.7). The full-year outlook was raised: sales growth of 6-8% in local currencies (previously 5-8%) and core operating profit growth of 10-13% (previously 7-10%).
risks: The sale of the Consumer Hearing business is not complete; no buyer or price has been announced. Further losses may be booked until it closes (56.8 million francs after tax in the first half).
Market share depends on the product cycle: if the new EON platform disappoints or rivals launch a better product, growth falls below the market. Large US buyers (VA, Costco) push prices down.

Restructuring, litigation and provision charges have recurred for three years; the company's "core" profit leaves them out. The provision for a legacy cochlear implant product was raised again (another 5.0 million francs in the first half).

The company grows through acquisitions and has paused buybacks for that reason; net debt is 1,072.4 million francs. We could not read the goodwill figure; expensive purchases lower the return on capital.
The company reports in francs while most sales are in other currencies; in the year to March 2026 sales rose 5.9% in local currencies but fell 0.2% in francs.

Fiyatlama gücü marjda görünür: brüt marj 2025'te %64, 2026'nın ilk yarısında %66,6; FAVÖK marjı 2024'te %31,2, 2025'te %30,0, 2026'nın ilk yarısında %29,0. Vana, makinenin tasarımına girer (2026'nın ilk yarısında 60 yeni tasarım kazanımı); sonra yıllarca aynı vana ve yedek parçası satılır. Servis kolunun FAVÖK marjı %47,2. Ar-Ge harcaması 2025'te 75 milyon frank (satışın %7'si). Bir rakibin bu güveni ve tasarım yerini kazanması yıllar ve büyük sermaye ister. Zayıf yanı: tek sektöre ve az sayıda makine üreticisine bağlılık; satışlar çip yatırımıyla sert oynar. 2022 enflasyon yılının brüt marjına ve en büyük müşterilerin payına bakıldı; okunan belgelerde yok.
VACN.mgmt: Kârın neredeyse tamamı temettüye gidiyor: 2025 için hisse başına 7,00 frank, toplam 209,8 milyon frank ödendi (net kâr 214,3 milyon frank; hisse başına kâr 7,15 frank). Geri alım yok. Borç makul: 30 Haziran 2026'da net borç 281,6 milyon frank, FAVÖK'ün 0,9 katı; özsermaye temettüden sonra 685,0 milyon frank. Emeklilik yükümlülüğü 21,2 milyon frank. Şirket tek seferlik kalem açıklamıyor. Ortaklık yapısına bakıldı; okunan belgelerde yok.

Sipariş 696,6 milyon frank (geçen yıl 238,1; +%192,6), net satış 376,4 milyon frank (+%45,9); ikisi de şirket tarihinin en yükseği. Dokuz ayda sipariş 1.553,0 milyon frank (+%113,5), net satış 888,3 milyon frank (+%8,9); bekleyen sipariş 979,5 milyon frank. Dördüncü çeyrek için 420-450 milyon frank net satış bekleniyor. en.one: The leader in vacuum valves for chip manufacturing, with about 70% market share. It passed Wall 3, but earnings depend on the chip investment cycle.
en.business: VAT makes the high-vacuum valves used in chip and display manufacturing equipment and sells service and spare parts for them. In 2025 net sales were 1,074 million francs, EBITDA 322 million francs (30.0%) and net income 214.3 million francs. In the first half of 2026 net sales were 511.9 million francs: Valves 406.2 (of which semiconductors 343.0) and Global Service 105.7 million francs. Direct sales to Chinese customers were 28% of first-half sales.
en.moat_text: The moat is wide. The company puts its market share in semiconductor vacuum valves at about 70%, unchanged from 2024 to 2025. Pricing power shows in the margin: gross margin was 64% in 2025 and 66.6% in the first half of 2026; EBITDA margin was 31.2% in 2024, 30.0% in 2025 and 29.0% in the first half of 2026. Real return on equity ranged from 22.7% to 39.5% over five years and averaged 30.0%. The valve is designed into the machine (60 new specification wins in the first half of 2026); the same valve and its spare parts then sell for years. The service segment's EBITDA margin is 47.2%. R&D spending was 75 million francs in 2025 (7% of sales). Winning that trust and those design slots would take a rival years and a lot of capital. The weak side: dependence on one industry and a small number of equipment makers; sales swing sharply with chip investment. We looked for gross margin in the 2022 inflation year and for the share of the largest customers; they are not in the documents read.
en.mgmt: Almost all profit goes to dividends: 7.00 francs per share for 2025, 209.8 million francs in total (net income 214.3 million francs; earnings per share 7.15 francs). There are no buybacks. Debt is moderate: net debt was 281.6 million francs at 30 June 2026, 0.9 times EBITDA; equity after the dividend was 685.0 million francs. On 22 July 2026 the company announced the purchase of the Japanese sensor company Atonarp for about 110 million francs; the deal is related to the core business (process monitoring in chip manufacturing) and will be paid for with a loan. Intangible assets and goodwill are 433.4 million francs (63% of equity). Share-based pay is small: 3.4 million francs after tax in 2025 (1.6% of net income). Pension obligations are 21.2 million francs. The company reports no one-off items. We looked for the shareholder structure; it is not in the documents read.
en.latest: 15 October 2026: The company published third-quarter figures. Orders were 696.6 million francs (238.1 a year earlier; +192.6%) and net sales 376.4 million francs (+45.9%); both are the highest in the company's history. Over nine months orders were 1,553.0 million francs (+113.5%) and net sales 888.3 million francs (+8.9%); the order backlog is 979.5 million francs. Net sales of 420-450 million francs are expected for the fourth quarter. The company expects 2026 orders, sales, EBITDA, net income and free cash flow to be above 2025, and says 2027 sales will be significantly above its previous guidance of 1.5-1.7 billion francs. First half, announced on 22 July 2026: net sales 511.9 million francs (−8.3%), net income 98.8 million francs (105.6) and earnings per share 3.30 francs (3.52).
risks: Earnings depend on the chip investment cycle: orders can triple in a year and fall just as sharply (real return on equity was 39.5% in 2022 and 22.7% in 2023). This is the strong side of the cycle; five years of history do not show a full cycle.
Direct sales to Chinese customers were 28% of first-half sales (about 35% a year earlier). Export restrictions or the rise of Chinese rivals could reduce them.

The customers are a small number of chip equipment makers; we could not find the share of the largest customers in the documents read. If a large customer makes its own valves or picks a second supplier, share falls.

The company reports in francs while most sales are linked to the dollar: in the first half of 2026 sales rose 0.1% at constant currency but fell 8.3% in francs. Currency and hedging effects added 1.8 points to the first-half EBITDA margin.
Rapid capacity expansion is risky: 709 people were added in six months, most of them temporary. If orders are postponed, the costs stay.

LOGN.business: Logitech bilgisayar fareleri, klavyeler, oyun donanımı, web kameraları ve görüntülü toplantı cihazları satar; dolarla raporlar ve mali yılı mart sonunda biter. Hisse bazlı ücret yüksek: mart 2026'da biten yılda 112 milyon dolar, net kârın %15,8'i. Şirketin "GAAP dışı" kârı bunu dışarıda bırakır; biz o ölçüyü kullanmıyoruz. Şerefiye 465 milyon dolar (özsermayenin %21'i); son yıllarda büyük alım yok. Yeniden yapılanma gideri küçük (altı ayda 0,9 milyon dolar). Net satış 1.218,8 milyon dolar (geçen yıl 1.186,1), faaliyet kârı 200,6 milyon dolar (191,3), net kâr 180,0 milyon dolar (170,7), seyreltilmiş hisse başına kâr 1,25 dolar (1,15). Bir çip tedarikçisinin fabrikası haziran sonunda kapanmıştı, eylülde kısmen açıldı; şirket aralık çeyreğinde bundan 70-80 milyon dolar satış kaybı bekliyor. en.one: A global brand in mice, keyboards and gaming gear, debt-free and cash-rich. It passed Wall 3; last-12-month profit includes a one-off tariff refund.
en.business: Logitech sells computer mice, keyboards, gaming gear, webcams and video conferencing devices; it reports in dollars and its fiscal year ends in March. In the year to March 2026 net sales were 4.84 billion dollars, operating income 775 million dollars and net income 711 million dollars. In the June 2026 quarter Gaming had sales of 354 million, Keyboards 228 million, Pointing Devices 227 million and Video Collaboration 185 million dollars. About 35% of products are made in the company's own factory in China and the rest by contract manufacturers in Asia and Mexico (fiscal 2025 report).
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow: brand, scale and shelf presence are real, but switching products is easy for the customer. Evidence: gross margin was 43.1% and 43.2% in the fiscal years to March 2025 and March 2026; the company says it gained about 320 basis points of global share in pointing devices and 280 in keyboards in the September 2026 quarter. A sign of pricing power: price increases in May 2026 covered rising component costs, and about 60% of the growth in video collaboration came from price. Real return on equity averaged 26.7% over five years. Why not wide: there are many rivals (Razer, Corsair, Apple, Microsoft, Dell, HP and low-priced Chinese brands); this is a consumer electronics business and profitability moves with waves of demand (real return on equity fell to 13.7% in the fiscal year to March 2023). For the December 2026 quarter the company expects gross margin to drop to 41-42% because of freight, component costs and promotions.
en.mgmt: There is no debt; at 30 September 2026 cash was 1,507.6 million dollars and equity 2,163.2 million dollars. Profit returns to owners: in the year to March 2026 the company bought back 535 million dollars of shares and paid 233 million dollars in dividends (768 million in total; net income 711 million dollars). In the six months to September 2026 it bought back 284.5 million dollars; the diluted share count fell from 149.1 million to 145.0 million in a year. We looked for the average buyback price; it is not in the documents read. Share-based pay is high: 112 million dollars in the year to March 2026, 15.8% of net income. The company's "non-GAAP" profit leaves it out; we do not use that measure. Goodwill is 465 million dollars (21% of equity); there has been no large acquisition in recent years. Restructuring charges are small (0.9 million dollars in six months). We looked for pension and off-balance-sheet obligations and the shareholder structure; they are not in the sections read.
en.latest: 27 October 2026: The company reported the September 2026 quarter. Net sales were 1,218.8 million dollars (1,186.1 a year earlier), operating income 200.6 million dollars (191.3), net income 180.0 million dollars (170.7) and diluted earnings per share 1.25 dollars (1.15). Over six months net income was 415.7 million dollars (316.7) and earnings per share 2.88 dollars (2.13); this includes 61 million dollars of tariff refunds booked against cost of goods sold in the June quarter. A chip supplier's plant closed at the end of June and partly reopened in September; the company expects it to cost 70-80 million dollars of sales in the December quarter. Outlook for the December quarter: net sales of 1,360-1,430 million dollars (between −4% and +1% in dollars).
risks: Last-12-month profit includes a one-off gain: 61 million dollars of tariff refunds (pre-tax) in the June 2026 quarter. Without it, six-month profit growth is lower; the company gives its full-year outlook excluding the refund.

The supply chain is fragile: an incident at a single chip supplier is costing 70-80 million dollars of sales in the December quarter. Memory and other component costs are rising; the company expects gross margin to fall by about 200 basis points in the December quarter.
Demand depends on consumer spending and the PC cycle; real return on equity fell to 13.7% in the fiscal year to March 2023. The five-year history also includes the pandemic-era wave of demand.

Sales are concentrated in a few large buyers: in the fiscal year to March 2025 Amazon was 19% of gross sales, Ingram Micro 14% and TD Synnex 12%. About 35% of production is in a single factory in China; tariffs directly affect costs.

The company reports in dollars while the shares trade in francs in Switzerland; the inflation adjustment uses Swiss inflation. Share-based pay is 15.8% of net income; part of the buyback goes to offset that dilution.
