en.one: The market leader in damper actuators, valves and sensors for building ventilation. The moat is wide; half of growth comes from data centres.
en.business: Belimo makes the small devices that regulate air and water in heating, ventilation and air-conditioning systems of buildings: damper actuators, control valves, sensors and meters. In 2025 net sales were 1,120.8 million francs, operating profit 232.9 million francs (20.8%) and net income 181.6 million francs. Control valves brought 591.4 million francs of sales, damper actuators 476.3 million and sensors and meters 53.1 million. By region: Americas 544.0, Europe-Middle East-Africa 429.4 and Asia Pacific 147.4 million francs.
en.moat_text: The moat is wide. The company describes itself as the market and innovation leader in these devices; the evidence shows in the margin and in the return on capital. The operating margin was 19.2% in 2024, 20.8% in 2025 and 22.5% in the first half of 2026. Real return on equity averaged 25.7% over five years; it was 20.4% in its lowest year and 33.2% over the last 12 months. Company-reported return on capital employed was 36.3% in 2025 (2024: 31.3%). Recent evidence of pricing power: according to the company, the impact of tariffs was eased by price increases in the second half of 2025, and the margin still rose. The product is a small part of a building's cost but expensive when it fails; customers look at reliability and lead times. The weak side: a market share figure, R&D spending and gross margin are not in the documents read; slightly less than half of 2025 growth and slightly more than half of growth in the first half of 2026 came from data centres. That demand depends on an investment cycle.
en.mgmt: The largest shareholder is Group Linsi: 19.55% of shares at 31 December 2025. UBS Fund Management holds 5.56% and BlackRock 5.18%. The company holds almost none of its own shares (0.0003%). Profit goes to the core business and to dividends: 10.00 francs per share for 2025 (2024: 9.50; earnings per share 14.77 francs). Capital spending rose for capacity expansion: 86.8 million francs in 2025 (2024: 63.1) and 45.4 million in the first half of 2026. At 30 June 2026 net debt was 27.7 million francs, equity 624.1 million francs and the equity ratio 61.2%. There is no goodwill line on the balance sheet; intangible assets are 23.0 million francs. The pension liability is 6.5 million francs. There are no options or similar dilutive instruments (half-year report). We looked for the amount of share-based pay, buybacks and off-balance-sheet commitments; they are not in the documents read. The company reported no one-off items in the last two years.
en.latest: 20 July 2026: The company published first-half results. Net sales were 676.4 million francs (+20.5% in francs, +29.6% in local currencies). Operating profit was 152.5 million francs (128.1), a margin of 22.5% (22.8%). Net income was 124.9 million francs (+23.3%) and earnings per share 10.15 francs (8.23). The Americas grew 35.1% in local currencies, Asia Pacific 58.0% and Europe-Middle East-Africa 14.1%. Free cash flow fell to 38.7 million francs (52.8) because of working capital and investment. The company expects an operating margin above 20% in 2026 and says growth will slow in the second half because of a higher base and the annualisation of price increases.
risks: Half of the growth comes from data-centre investment (slightly more than half in the first half of 2026). If that investment slows, profit growth falls quickly; the company already expects a slowdown in the second half.

The company is expanding capacity for this demand: capital spending rose for two years and free cash flow fell 25.8% in 2025 (98.5 million francs). If the demand does not come, the new capacity lowers returns.
Half of sales come from the Americas (50% in the first half of 2026). A weaker dollar lowers profit in francs; currency cut about nine points from first-half growth. Tariffs raise costs.
The price requires high growth to continue: the share trades at about 46 times the profit of the last 12 months.

en.one: A Swiss group that wins clients through retirement advice, then manages their assets. The moat is narrow but proven; the founder holds 61%.
en.business: VZ Group gives fee-based retirement, tax and estate advice to people over 50; after the advice most clients have their assets managed on VZ's platforms. The company has its own custody bank. In 2025 total revenues were 574.5 million francs and net profit 236.4 million francs; 382.1 million francs of revenue came from assets under management. Assets under management were 67.7 billion francs at 30 June 2026. It had 94,433 clients at the end of 2025. Besides Switzerland it has branches in Germany and the United Kingdom.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow: real and proven by numbers, but tied to one model and one country. The client first pays a fee for advice and then brings assets; this order differs from rivals' product-led model and keeps clients for years. Evidence: net new money was 5.1 billion francs in 2024, 5.8 billion in 2025 and 3.3 billion in the first half of 2026; assets under management rose 19.8% in a year. Real return on equity averaged 20.1% over five years and was 17.3% in its lowest year; the company achieves this with high capital (core capital ratio 28.4%). Operating profit was 48% of revenue in the first half of 2026 (153.1 ÷ 316.5 million francs). Why not wide: banks and independent advisers can offer the same service; two thirds of revenue are management fees tied to market values; banking income fell 10.1% in 2025 as interest rates fell. We looked for the trend of fee rates over the years; it is not in the documents read.
en.mgmt: Founder Matthias Reinhart holds 61.19% of the shares directly and indirectly (30 June 2026); employees hold 4.79% and the company's own shares are 1.54%. The free float is small; minority shareholders depend on the founder's decisions. Half of the profit goes to dividends: 2.95 francs per share for 2025 (2024: 2.73), 50% of net profit. The rest builds capital: equity was 1,207.3 million francs at 30 June 2026 and total assets 8,762.5 million francs (equity ratio 13.8%). In May and June 2026 the minority stakes in the UK firms Lumin Group and Davidson Deem were bought for about 30.3 million francs in total; this is core business and small. The company reported no one-off items in its 2025 results. We looked for share-based pay, goodwill, credit quality and off-balance-sheet commitments; they are not in the documents read (the half-year report itself could not be opened).
en.latest: 14 August 2026: The company published first-half results. Total revenues were 316.5 million francs (277.9; +13.9%), operating profit 153.1 million francs (130.0) and net profit 131.9 million francs (112.0; +17.7%). Revenue from assets under management rose 18.2% to 216.6 million francs. Net new money was 3.3 billion francs (3.0) and assets under management 67.7 billion francs (end of 2025: 61.8). The core capital ratio was 28.4% and the leverage ratio 10.8%. Management expects second-half growth similar to the first half if markets stay stable and says the dividend will rise with profit.
risks: About two thirds of revenue depend on the value of assets under management. If markets fall sharply, revenue and profit fall together; 2.6 billion francs of the first-half rise in assets was market performance.
Banking income shrinks when interest rates fall: it declined 10.1% in 2025. While Swiss rates stay low, this line slows growth.
The business model rests on Switzerland's pension system and tax rules. If the rules on withdrawing pension capital change, demand for advice and inflows are affected.
The founder holds 61% of the shares; the free float is small. The price also requires growth to continue: the share trades at about 28 times the profit of the last 12 months.

ACLN.business: Accelleron, gemilerin ve elektrik santrallerinin büyük dizel ve gaz motorlarına turboşarj ve yakıt enjeksiyon sistemi üretir, sonra bunların bakımını yapar. 2025'te gelir 1.263,1 milyon dolar, şirketin tanımıyla faaliyet kârı (operational EBITA) 321,0 milyon dolar (%25,4), net kâr 243,7 milyon dolar oldu. Enerji, gelirin %40'ından fazlasıdır. 100'den fazla noktada 500'den fazla servis mühendisi 5.000'den fazla müşteriye hizmet verir. Şirket dolar cinsinden raporlar; hissesi frankla işlem görür.

Şirket kendini kritik uygulamalarda turboşarjın "tartışmasız lideri" diye tanımlıyor; denizcilikte "önemli" bir pay tuttuğunu söylüyor ama rakam vermiyor. Kanıt marjın istikrarında: operational EBITA marjı 2024'te %25,6, 2025'te %25,4, 2026'nın ilk yarısında %25,7; gümrük vergilerine rağmen korundu. Motor 20-30 yıl çalışır; kurulu turboşarjın bakımı ve yedek parçası üreticiye bağlıdır, servis ağını kurmak yıllar ister. AR-GE gelirin %5'inden fazladır (2025: 67,9 milyon dolar). Reel özsermaye kârlılığı beş yılda ortalama %49,7, en düşük yılında %34,4; ama özsermaye küçük (30 Haziran 2026: 428,8 milyon dolar) ve kârın çoğu dağıtıldığı için oran olduğundan yüksek görünür. Neden geniş değil: servis gelirinin payı ve kurulu taban okunan belgelerde yok; müşteriler az sayıda motor üreticisidir; uzun vadede içten yanmalı motorun yerini başka teknolojiler alabilir.
ACLN.mgmt: Hâkim ortak yok: UBS Fund Management %5,06, BlackRock %5,06, Swisscanto %4,99, Norges Bank %3,46 (2025 sonu). en.one: A leader in making and servicing turbochargers for ship and power-plant engines. The moat is real but tied to the cycle; it reports in dollars.
en.business: Accelleron makes turbochargers and fuel-injection systems for the large diesel and gas engines of ships and power plants, and then services them. In 2025 revenue was 1,263.1 million dollars, operating profit on the company's definition (operational EBITA) 321.0 million dollars (25.4%) and net income 243.7 million dollars. There are two segments: Medium & Low Speed with 929.6 million dollars and High Speed with 333.5 million dollars. Energy is more than 40% of revenue. More than 500 service engineers in over 100 locations serve more than 5,000 customers. The company reports in dollars; its share trades in francs.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow: real and visible in the margin, but the market share could not be confirmed with a number and demand is cyclical. The company calls itself the "undisputed leader" in turbocharging for mission-critical applications and says it holds a "substantial" share in marine, without a figure. The evidence is the stability of the margin: operational EBITA margin was 25.6% in 2024, 25.4% in 2025 and 25.7% in the first half of 2026; it held despite tariffs. An engine runs for 20-30 years; service and spare parts for an installed turbocharger depend on the maker, and a service network takes years to build. R&D is more than 5% of revenue (2025: 67.9 million dollars). Real return on equity averaged 49.7% over five years and was 34.4% in its lowest year; but equity is small (428.8 million dollars at 30 June 2026) and most profit is paid out, so the ratio looks higher than it is. Why not wide: the share of service revenue and the installed base are not in the documents read; the customers are a small number of engine makers; in the long run other technologies may replace the combustion engine.
en.mgmt: There is no controlling shareholder: UBS Fund Management 5.06%, BlackRock 5.06%, Swisscanto 4.99%, Norges Bank 3.46% (end of 2025). Most of the profit goes to shareholders: a dividend of 1.50 francs per share for 2025 (2024: 1.25); the amount paid in May 2026 was 178.9 million dollars. A two-year buyback of 100 million francs began in May 2026; in the first half 84,384 shares were bought for 8.5 million dollars (the price is not clear in the document). Acquisitions are in the core business and small: 58.8 million dollars for OMC2 and True North Marine in 2024; none in 2025. Goodwill is 78.9 million dollars (end of 2025; 17% of equity). Share-based pay was 3.8 million dollars in 2025 (1.6% of net income). The company's adjusted profit strips out "non-operational" costs every year: 18.6 million dollars in 2024, 12.3 in 2025 and 1.4 in the first half of 2026; because they recur, they should be treated as ordinary costs. Net debt is 278.9 million dollars and company-reported leverage 0.7 times. The pension plan is in surplus (77.2 million dollars of assets, 9.1 million of liabilities). Guarantees total 10.0 million dollars.
en.latest: 27 August 2026: The company published first-half results. Revenue was 737.3 million dollars (608.0; +17.2% organic). Operational EBITA was 189.7 million dollars (154.9), a margin of 25.7%. Net income attributable to the parent was 143.9 million dollars (109.7) and earnings per share 1.53 dollars (1.17). The High Speed segment grew 35.5% organically; the share of data-centre-related revenue rose from 5% to slightly below 9%. Capital spending was 31 million dollars, more than 40% above a year earlier; free cash flow was 88.1 million dollars (80.6). The company raised its 2026 organic growth guidance from 9-14% to 14-17%; the margin guidance stayed at 25-26%.
risks: Earnings depend on the cycle: new turbocharger sales rest on ship orders and power-plant investment, and recent growth on data centres' demand for backup power. Five years do not show a full cycle; these are good years.
The company reports in dollars and the share trades in francs. If the dollar weakens against the franc, profit and dividends in francs fall; the inflation adjustment uses Swiss inflation.
Equity is small and there is debt: at 30 June 2026 equity was 428.8 million dollars and net debt 278.9 million dollars. Part of the high return on equity comes from this structure.
If other technologies replace the combustion engine in shipping and energy over the long run, the installed base shrinks.
The customers are a small number of engine makers; a concentration figure is not in the documents read. Tariffs weigh on the margin of the High Speed segment.

en.one: An industrial group making precision metal parts and fasteners and distributing tools. It has an edge but no narrow moat; it fails wall 3.
en.business: SFS runs three businesses. Engineered Components makes customer-specific precision parts for automotive, electronics and medical-device makers (first-half 2026 sales 577.8 million francs). Fastening Systems sells fasteners for construction (293.8 million francs). Distribution & Logistics distributes tools and consumables under the Hoffmann brand (687.7 million francs). In 2025 sales were 3,056.6 million francs, operating profit 324.3 million francs and net income 220.2 million francs. Industrial manufacturing took 27.0% of sales, automotive 20.5% and construction 20.2%; 29.7% came from Germany.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak, which is why the company fails wall 3. The edge is real: there is engineering know-how in customer-specific parts, no customer exceeds 10% of sales, and the adjusted operating margin was 12.2% in 2025 and 13.3% in the first half of 2026. But this margin does not show lasting pricing power: nearly half of sales are distribution and construction fasteners (margins of 11-12%), demand follows the automotive and industrial cycle, and net income fell two years running (2024: 242.7; 2025: 220.2 million francs). Return on equity also looks higher than it is: under Swiss accounting rules (Swiss GAAP FER) the company offsets goodwill against equity. At 30 June 2026 goodwill offset against equity was 1,630.8 million francs, while equity itself was 1,583.9 million francs. According to the company's own note, if goodwill were capitalised and amortised, 2025 net income would have been 128.4 million francs instead of 220.2 million. The real return on equity on this page (15.9% on average over five years, 13.7% in 2025) is therefore above the true return of the business.
en.mgmt: Capital allocation is neutral. The dividend has been 2.50 francs per share for three years (2025 payout ratio 44.4%). Growth comes through acquisitions: in the first half of 2026 the company paid 202.1 million francs for three Hoffmann partner companies, Jellypipe and Harald Zahn, and offset 106.5 million francs of goodwill against equity; in July 2026 it signed a deal for US-based Heartland Precision Fasteners. The purchases are in the core business, but because goodwill does not appear on the balance sheet their returns cannot be followed. Restructuring costs recur: the programme to streamline the production and distribution network cost 46.7 million francs in 2025, and a net gain of 5.2 million francs was booked in the first half of 2026. Share-based pay is small (2025: 1.8 million francs). The balance sheet is sound: equity ratio 58.9%, net debt 320.4 million francs. Off-balance-sheet commitments are 334.5 million francs (end of 2025). The pension fund's coverage ratio is 117.5%. We looked for the shareholder structure; it is not in the documents read.
en.latest: 23 July 2026: The company published first-half results. Sales were 1,559.3 million francs (+1.3%; organic +4.0%, currency effect −4.2%). Adjusted operating profit was 206.0 million francs (168.1), a margin of 13.3% (11.0%); reported operating profit was 211.2 million francs (162.2). Net income attributable to shareholders was 148.6 million francs (111.2) and earnings per share 3.82 francs (2.86). The adjusted margin of the distribution segment rose from 8.2% to 11.8%. The company kept its 2026 guidance: sales growth of 3-6% in local currencies and an adjusted operating margin of 12-15%.
risks: Earnings depend on the automotive, industrial and construction cycles; net income fell in 2024 and 2025.
Because goodwill is offset against equity, return on equity and price-to-book flatter the true return of the business.
29.7% of sales come from Germany; weakness in European industry hits the distribution segment directly.

SQN.one: İsviçre'nin önde gelen çevrimiçi yatırım bankası. Hendek dar ama kanıtlı; son 12 ay kârında tek seferlik Yuh kazancı var ve şirket 2026 hedefini indirdi.
SQN.business: Swissquote, bireylere çevrimiçi hisse, fon, döviz ve kripto varlık alım satımı ile banka hesabı sunan lisanslı bir İsviçre bankasıdır. Para üç yerden gelir: işlem komisyonları, müşteri nakdinden kazanılan faiz ve döviz ile kripto işlemlerindeki fark. 2025'te net gelir 723,3 milyon frank, vergi öncesi kâr 420,2 milyon frank, net kâr 366,4 milyon frank oldu. Net faiz geliri 217,6 milyon frank (gelirin %30'u), kripto geliri 85,7 milyon frank (%12) idi. 30 Haziran 2026'da 1.220.818 hesap ve 96,3 milyar frank müşteri varlığı vardı. Temmuz 2025'ten beri Yuh uygulamasının tamamı şirketindir.
SQN.moat_text: Hendek dar sınıfta: gerçek ve rakamla kanıtlı, ama kazancın önemli bölümü piyasa hareketine ve faize bağlı. Kanıt ölçek ve maliyet üstünlüğünde: vergi öncesi kâr marjı 2025'te %58 (tek seferlik kazançla), 2026'nın ilk yarısında %50,2. Müşteri varlığı bir yılda %19,8 arttı; ilk yarıda net yeni para 5,1 milyar frank, 64.011 yeni hesap. Banka lisansı, kendi teknolojisi ve tanınan marka yeni girenin kısa sürede kuramayacağı şeylerdir. Reel özsermaye kârlılığı beş yılda ortalama %27,0, en düşük yılında (2022) %19,8. Neden geniş değil: komisyonlar rakiplerce aşağı çekilebilir; müşteri varlığını başka bankaya taşıyabilir; gelir çizgileri oynaktır. 2026'nın ilk yarısında kripto geliri %66,2 düşerek 14,6 milyon franka indi; 2025'te net faiz geliri %3,0 geriledi. Komisyon oranlarının yıllar içindeki seyrine bakıldı; okunan belgelerde yok.
SQN.mgmt: Halka açıklık oranı %78,5 (2025 sonu, SIX tanımı); ortakların adlarına bakıldı, okunan belgelerde yok. Kârın yaklaşık %30'u temettüye gidiyor: 2025 için hisse başına 7,40 frank (bölünme öncesi; 2024: 6,00), 2026'nın ilk yarısında ödenen tutar 110,2 milyon frank. Kalan kâr sermayede kalıp büyümeyi taşıyor: sermaye oranı %25,2. Geri alım hızlandı: ilk yarıda 56,9 milyon franklık kendi payı alındı (bir yıl önce 28,1); fiyatı belgede yok. Mayıs 2026'da hisse bire on bölündü (15.328.170 pay 153.281.700 oldu); bu yalnız pay sayısını değiştirir. Satın alma ana işle ilgili: Yuh'un kalan %50'si Temmuz 2025'te PostFinance'tan alındı; eldeki payın yeniden değerlenmesi 61,9 milyon frank tek seferlik kazanç yazdırdı. Şerefiye 154,9 milyon frank (özsermayenin %11'i). Hisse opsiyonu gideri ilk yarıda 3,9 milyon frank (net kârın %2,5'i). Net emeklilik yükümlülüğü 4,7 milyon frank. Kredi zararı gideri küçük: ilk yarıda 0,7 milyon frank; krediler 1.941,6 milyon frank. Sorunlu kredi oranına ve bilanço dışı yükümlülüklere bakıldı; yarıyıl raporunda yok.
SQN.latest: 13 Ağustos 2026: Şirket ilk yarı sonuçlarını açıkladı ve yıl hedefini indirdi. Net gelir 364,2 milyon frank (+%1,7), vergi öncesi kâr 182,9 milyon frank (185,2; −%1,2), net kâr 153,6 milyon frank (158,2; −%2,9), hisse başına kâr 1,03 frank (1,06). Net faiz geliri %7,2 artarak 115,9 milyon frank oldu; kripto geliri %66,2 düştü (14,6 milyon frank; içinde 5,3 milyon franklık değerleme zararı var). Giderler %4,6 arttı (181,3 milyon frank). 2026 hedefi: net gelir yaklaşık 730 milyon frank (önce 760), vergi öncesi kâr yaklaşık 365 milyon frank (önce 385; 2025'te 420,2). 2028 için 500 milyon franklık vergi öncesi kâr hedefi değişmedi. 30 Haziran 2026'da özsermaye 1.391,0 milyon frank, bilanço 16,9 milyar frank.
risks: Son 12 ayın kârı olağan kazancı olduğundan yüksek gösterir: 2025'in ikinci yarısında Yuh payının yeniden değerlenmesinden 61,9 milyon frank tek seferlik kazanç yazıldı; şirkete göre tek seferliklerin net etkisi yaklaşık 50 milyon frank. Şirket 2026 için 365 milyon frank vergi öncesi kâr bekliyor; 2025'te 420,2 milyon franktı.
Kazanç piyasa hareketine bağlı: müşteri az işlem yaparsa ya da kripto piyasası durgunlaşırsa gelir düşer. Kripto geliri 2026'nın ilk yarısında %66,2 geriledi.
Gelirin yaklaşık üçte biri net faiz geliridir (2026'nın ilk yarısında 115,9 milyon frank). İsviçre'de ve dolar ile avroda faizler düşerse bu gelir azalır.
Şirket bir bankadır: 30 Haziran 2026'da özsermaye bilançonun %8,2'si. Bilanço 17 milyar frankı geçince FINMA şirketi 3. kategori banka sayacak; sermaye ve denetim yükü artar.
Giderler gelirden hızlı artıyor (ilk yarıda %4,6'ya karşı %1,7); Yuh'un tam konsolidasyonu yaklaşık 50 milyon franklık itfa edilecek maddi olmayan varlık getirdi.

en.one: Switzerland's leading online investment bank. The moat is narrow but proven; trailing profit includes a one-off Yuh gain, and the 2026 target was cut.
en.business: Swissquote is a licensed Swiss bank that offers individuals online trading in shares, funds, currencies and crypto assets, plus bank accounts. Money comes from three places: trading commissions, interest earned on client cash, and the spread on currency and crypto trades. In 2025 net revenues were 723.3 million francs, pre-tax profit 420.2 million francs and net profit 366.4 million francs. Net interest income was 217.6 million francs (30% of revenue) and crypto income 85.7 million francs (12%). At 30 June 2026 it had 1,220,818 accounts and 96.3 billion francs of client assets. Since July 2025 it has owned all of the Yuh app.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow: real and proven by numbers, but a large part of earnings depends on market activity and interest rates. The evidence is scale and cost advantage: the pre-tax margin was 58% in 2025 (with the one-off gain) and 50.2% in the first half of 2026. Client assets rose 19.8% in a year; in the first half net new money was 5.1 billion francs with 64,011 new accounts. A banking licence, in-house technology and a known brand are things a newcomer cannot build quickly. Real return on equity averaged 27.0% over five years and was 19.8% in its lowest year (2022). Why not wide: rivals can push commissions down; clients can move their assets to another bank; the revenue lines are volatile. In the first half of 2026 crypto income fell 66.2% to 14.6 million francs; in 2025 net interest income fell 3.0%. We looked for the trend of commission rates over the years; it is not in the documents read.
en.mgmt: The free float is 78.5% (end of 2025, SIX definition); we looked for the names of shareholders, and they are not in the documents read. About 30% of profit goes to dividends: 7.40 francs per share for 2025 (pre-split; 2024: 6.00), with 110.2 million francs paid in the first half of 2026. The rest stays in capital and carries growth: the capital ratio is 25.2%. Buybacks have accelerated: 56.9 million francs of own shares were bought in the first half (28.1 a year earlier); the price is not in the document. In May 2026 the share was split one for ten (15,328,170 shares became 153,281,700); this changes only the share count. The acquisition is in the core business: the remaining 50% of Yuh was bought from PostFinance in July 2025; remeasuring the stake already held produced a one-off gain of 61.9 million francs. Goodwill is 154.9 million francs (11% of equity). Share option expense was 3.9 million francs in the first half (2.5% of net profit). The net pension liability is 4.7 million francs. Credit loss expense is small: 0.7 million francs in the first half; loans are 1,941.6 million francs. We looked for the impaired-loan ratio and off-balance-sheet commitments; they are not in the half-year report.
en.latest: 13 August 2026: The company published first-half results and cut its full-year target. Net revenues were 364.2 million francs (+1.7%), pre-tax profit 182.9 million francs (185.2; −1.2%), net profit 153.6 million francs (158.2; −2.9%) and earnings per share 1.03 francs (1.06). Net interest income rose 7.2% to 115.9 million francs; crypto income fell 66.2% (14.6 million francs, including a valuation loss of 5.3 million francs). Expenses rose 4.6% (181.3 million francs). The 2026 target: net revenues of about 730 million francs (previously 760) and pre-tax profit of about 365 million francs (previously 385; 420.2 in 2025). The 2028 target of 500 million francs of pre-tax profit is unchanged. At 30 June 2026 equity was 1,391.0 million francs and total assets 16.9 billion francs.
risks: The profit of the last 12 months overstates ordinary earnings: a one-off gain of 61.9 million francs from remeasuring the Yuh stake was booked in the second half of 2025; according to the company the net effect of one-offs was about 50 million francs. The company expects pre-tax profit of 365 million francs for 2026, against 420.2 million in 2025.
Earnings depend on market activity: if clients trade less or the crypto market goes quiet, revenue falls. Crypto income fell 66.2% in the first half of 2026.
About one third of revenue is net interest income (115.9 million francs in the first half of 2026). If interest rates fall in Switzerland and on the dollar and euro, this income shrinks.
The company is a bank: at 30 June 2026 equity was 8.2% of total assets. Once total assets pass 17 billion francs, FINMA will treat it as a category 3 bank; capital and supervisory demands increase.
Expenses are growing faster than revenue (4.6% against 1.7% in the first half); the full consolidation of Yuh brought about 50 million francs of intangible assets to be amortised.

basis.tr: Hesap son 12 ayın kârına dayanır. Bu kârın içindeki tek seferlik kazançlar: Yuh'un kalan %50'si alınırken eldeki %50 payın gerçeğe uygun değerle yeniden ölçülmesinden doğan kazanç: 61,9 milyon frank (2025'in ikinci yarısı; Yuh 4 Temmuz 2025'te tam konsolide edildi): son 12 ay kârının %17,1 kadarı. Aynı dönemin tek seferlik giderleri: 2025'in öbür tek seferlik kalemleri (gider): şirket tek seferliklerin net etkisini +49,8 milyon frank diye açıkladı; 61,9 − 49,8 = 12,1 milyon frank. Kalemlerin dökümü okunan belgelerde yok: %3,3. Net etki %13,8; kazanç bu kadar indirildi. Son 12 ayın kârı 0,86 ile çarpılarak kullanıldı.
basis.en: The calculation rests on the profit of the last 12 months. One-off gains inside that profit: Gain on remeasuring at fair value the 50% Yuh stake already held when the remaining 50% was bought: 61.9 million francs (second half of 2025; Yuh fully consolidated on 4 July 2025): 17.1% of last-12-month profit. One-off charges in the same period: Other one-off items of 2025 (charges): the company gave the net effect of one-offs as +49.8 million francs; 61.9 − 49.8 = 12.1 million francs. The breakdown is not in the documents read: 3.3%. The net effect is 13.8%; earnings were lowered by that much. Last-12-month profit was used multiplied by 0.86.

Bu, formülün hızının yarısından az olduğu için ikisinin ortası alındı: %7,2.
basis.en: The formula gave growth of 14.4% a year. Latest figures (earnings per share, year on year): January-June 2026 (first half) −2.8%; company target for 2026 (pre-tax profit) −13.1%. The company cut its 2026 target on 13 August 2026; crypto income fell 66.2% in the first half. The lowest, after inflation, is 0.0% (below zero counts as zero). Because this is less than half the formula's rate, the midpoint of the two was used: 7.2%.

EMMN.one: İsviçre'nin en büyük süt işleyicisi; peynir, hazır kahve ve tatlı satar. Markaları var ama marjı ince; 3. surda elendi.
EMMN.business: Emmi süt alır, işler ve satar: peynir, yoğurt, hazır soğuk kahve, keçi sütü ürünleri ve tatlılar. 2025'te net satış 4.745,7 milyon frank, faaliyet kârı 334,6 milyon frank (%7,1), net kâr 227,1 milyon frank (%4,8) oldu. 2026'nın ilk yarısında satışın 903,3 milyon frankı İsviçre'den, 852,8 milyon frankı Amerika kıtasından, 498,3 milyon frankı Avrupa'dan geldi. Fransız tatlı üreticisi Mademoiselle Desserts Ekim 2024'te gruba katıldı.
EMMN.moat_text: Hendek zayıf sınıfta; şirket bu yüzden 3. surda eleniyor. Üstünlük var: İsviçre'de ölçek, tanınan markalar ve bazı niş ürünlerde güçlü konum; organik büyüme 2025'te %4,3, 2026'nın ilk yarısında %3,6 ve tamamı hacimden. Ama rakamlar kalıcı bir fiyatlama gücünü göstermiyor. Faaliyet kâr marjı %7 dolayında (2025: %7,1; 2026 ilk yarı: %6,6), net kâr marjı %4,3-4,8. Şirketin açıkladığı yatırılan sermaye getirisi 2025'te %7,6 (2024: %8,6), 2026'nın ilk yarısında %7,9; kendi orta vadeli hedefi olan %10'un altında. Ana girdi süttür; süt fiyatı değişince satış fiyatı da değişir. 2022'de maliyetler yükselince reel özsermaye kârlılığı %12,3'e indi. Özsermaye kârlılığı ayrıca olduğundan yüksek görünür: şirket İsviçre muhasebe kuralları (Swiss GAAP FER) gereği şerefiyeyi özsermayeden düşer. 30 Haziran 2026'da özsermayeden düşülmüş birikimli şerefiye 1.474,4 milyon frank, ana ortaklığa ait özsermaye 1.095,0 milyon frank. Sayfadaki reel özsermaye kârlılığı (beş yılda ortalama %17,0) bu yüzden işin gerçek getirisinin üstündedir.
EMMN.mgmt: Hâkim ortak süt üreticileridir: ZMP Invest (Orta İsviçre süt üreticileri) payların %53,4'ünü, peynir ustaları kooperatifi %4,0'ını tutar. Şirketin süt aldığı çiftçiler aynı zamanda hâkim ortağıdır; süt fiyatında çıkarları küçük ortakla aynı değildir. Ortaklar grubu 7 Kasım 2025'te dağıldığını bildirdi. Temettü 2025 için hisse başına 17,50 frank (2024: 16,50; dağıtım oranı %41,2). Büyüme satın almayla geldi ve getiriyi düşürdü: Mademoiselle Desserts sonrası 2025'te amortisman 127,9 milyondan 157,6 milyon franka çıktı, şirketin açıkladığı sermaye getirisi geriledi. Net borç 862,4 milyon frank, FAVÖK'ün 1,73 katı (şirketin açıkladığı). Azınlık payları kârın önemli bölümünü alıyor: ilk yarıda 113,2 milyon frankın 12,3 milyonu. 2026'nın ilk yarısında tek seferlik kalem yok (yarıyıl raporu). Hisse bazlı ücrete, kendi paylarına ve emeklilik yükümlülüğüne bakıldı; okunan belgelerde yok.
EMMN.latest: 19 Ağustos 2026: Şirket ilk yarı sonuçlarını açıkladı. Net satış 2.323,5 milyon frank (+%2,2; organik +%3,6, kur etkisi −%2,1). Brüt marj %40,8 (%40,0). Faaliyet kârı 152,3 milyon frank (145,4), marj %6,6. Net kâr 100,9 milyon frank (97,2; +%3,7), hisse başına kâr 18,85 frank (18,18). Şerefiye özsermayeden düşüldüğü için özsermaye kârlılığı ve PD/DD işin gerçek getirisini olduğundan iyi gösterir.

en.one: Switzerland's largest milk processor, selling cheese, ready-to-drink coffee and desserts. It has brands but thin margins; it fails wall 3.
en.business: Emmi buys milk, processes it and sells it: cheese, yogurt, ready-to-drink cold coffee, goat's milk products and desserts. In 2025 net sales were 4,745.7 million francs, operating profit 334.6 million francs (7.1%) and net profit 227.1 million francs (4.8%). In the first half of 2026, 903.3 million francs of sales came from Switzerland, 852.8 million from the Americas and 498.3 million from Europe. The French dessert maker Mademoiselle Desserts joined the group in October 2024.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak, which is why the company fails wall 3. There is an edge: scale in Switzerland, known brands and a strong position in some niche products; organic growth was 4.3% in 2025 and 3.6% in the first half of 2026, all of it from volume. But the numbers do not show lasting pricing power. The operating margin is around 7% (2025: 7.1%; first half 2026: 6.6%) and the net margin 4.3-4.8%. Company-reported return on invested capital was 7.6% in 2025 (2024: 8.6%) and 7.9% in the first half of 2026, below its own mid-term target of 10%. The main input is milk; when the milk price changes, selling prices change too. When costs rose in 2022, real return on equity fell to 12.3%. Return on equity also looks higher than it is: under Swiss accounting rules (Swiss GAAP FER) the company offsets goodwill against equity. At 30 June 2026 cumulative goodwill offset against equity was 1,474.4 million francs, while equity attributable to shareholders was 1,095.0 million francs. The real return on equity on this page (17.0% on average over five years) is therefore above the true return of the business.
en.mgmt: The controlling shareholders are milk producers: ZMP Invest (Central Switzerland milk producers) holds 53.4% of the shares and the cheesemakers' cooperative 4.0%. The farmers who sell milk to the company are also its controlling shareholder; on the milk price their interest is not the same as the minority's. The shareholder group announced its dissolution on 7 November 2025. The dividend for 2025 is 17.50 francs per share (2024: 16.50; payout ratio 41.2%). Growth came through acquisitions and lowered returns: after Mademoiselle Desserts, depreciation and amortisation rose from 127.9 million to 157.6 million francs in 2025 and company-reported return on capital fell. Net debt is 862.4 million francs, 1.73 times EBITDA (company-reported). Minority interests take a meaningful part of profit: 12.3 million of 113.2 million francs in the first half. There were no non-recurring items in the first half of 2026 (half-year report). We looked for share-based pay, treasury shares and pension obligations; they are not in the documents read.
en.latest: 19 August 2026: The company published first-half results. Net sales were 2,323.5 million francs (+2.2%; organic +3.6%, currency effect −2.1%). The gross margin was 40.8% (40.0%). Operating profit was 152.3 million francs (145.4), a margin of 6.6%. Net profit was 100.9 million francs (97.2; +3.7%) and earnings per share 18.85 francs (18.18). The company raised its 2026 organic growth guidance to 2-3% (previously 1-3%); the operating profit guidance stayed at 335-355 million francs and the net margin guidance at 4.8-5.3%.
risks: Margins are thin: the operating margin is around 7%. If milk, energy or packaging costs rise and cannot be passed on, profit falls quickly.
Because goodwill is offset against equity, return on equity and price-to-book flatter the true return of the business.
A large part of sales comes from outside Switzerland; a weaker dollar and euro lower sales and profit in francs (currency effect of −2.1% in the first half).

CFT.one: Bankalar arasında faiz, döviz ve emtia işlemlerine aracılık eden küresel aracı kurum. Hendek dar: ölçek ve ağ var, ama kâr piyasa oynaklığına ve aracılara bağlı.
CFT.business: Compagnie Financière Tradition bankalar ve kurumlar arasında faiz, döviz, tahvil, hisse türevi ve emtia işlemlerine aracılık eder; her işlemden komisyon alır. 30'dan fazla ülkede çalışır; 2025 sonunda 2.470 çalışanı vardı. 2025'te ortak girişimler dahil gelir 1.203,6 milyon frank, faaliyet kârı 187,4 milyon frank oldu. Japonya'da bireysel döviz işlemleri yapan Gaitame.com ortak girişimdir. Personel gideri gelirin yaklaşık %69'udur (771,2 milyon frank; gelir 1.115,8 milyon).
CFT.moat_text: Hendek dar. Üstünlük ölçekten ve ağdan gelir: alıcı ile satıcı en çok hangi aracıda buluşuyorsa işlem oraya gider. Şirket kendini sektörün az sayıdaki gerçekten küresel oyuncusundan biri olarak tanımlıyor. Rakamlarda görünüyor: ortak girişimler dahil faaliyet marjı 2024'te %13,4, 2025'te %15,6, 2026'nın ilk yarısında %16,8; reel özsermaye kârlılığı beş yılda %15,4'ten %27,9'a çıktı, son 12 ayda %28,8. Zayıf yanlar: gelirin yaklaşık %69'u çalışanlara gidiyor, yani kazancın büyük bölümü aracıların elinde; hacim faiz ve oynaklık ortamına bağlı; elektronik platformlar sesli aracılığı zorluyor. Pazar payı rakamı okunan belgelerde yok. Bu yüzden geniş değil, dar.
CFT.mgmt: Şirketi VIEL & Cie kontrol ediyor: sermayenin %68,94'ü. Başka hiçbir ortağın oy hakkı %3'ü geçmiyor. Kâr temettüye, geri alıma ve özsermayeye gidiyor: 2025 için hisse başına 7,50 frank temettü (%11,1 artış; 28 Mayıs 2026'da 57,1 milyon frank ödendi); 2025'te 114.238 hisse 26,9 milyon franka geri alındı (hisse başına yaklaşık 236 frank) ve 142.183 hisse iptal edildi. 30 Haziran 2026'da 7.965.636 hisse çıkarılmış, 363.988'i şirketin elinde. Kusur: 2025 sonunda 373.605 hisse opsiyonu vardı (çıkarılmış hisselerin yaklaşık %4,7'si); seyreltilmiş hisse başına kâr temel rakamın yaklaşık %5 altında (2026 ilk yarı: 9,95 ve 10,43 frank). Hisse bazlı ücret gideri küçük: 2025'te 2,0 milyon frank, 2026'nın ilk yarısında 2,1 milyon. Şerefiye 34,3 milyon frank, ana ortaklık özsermayesinin %7'si; son iki yılda değer düşüklüğü yok. Yinelenen yeniden yapılanma giderine bakıldı, okunan belgelerde yok.
CFT.latest: 28 Ağustos 2026: Şirket 2026'nın ilk yarısında 79,1 milyon frank ana ortaklık kârı açıkladı (geçen yıl 70,2 milyon; +%12,6, sabit kurla +%22,5). Hisse başına kâr 10,43 frank (9,14); seyreltilmiş 9,95 frank (8,80). Gelir 597,8 milyon frank (+%3,1; sabit kurla +%11,0). Faaliyet kârı 88,0 milyon frank ile yatay kaldı (88,2); marj %14,7 (%15,2). Artış faaliyet dışından geldi: iştirak ve ortak girişimlerin payı 12,1 milyon franktan 16,1 milyona çıktı, kur zararı azaldı, vergi oranı %26,1'den %23,4'e indi. Ana ortaklığa ait özsermaye 493,3 milyon frank. Şirket rakamla beklenti vermedi.
risks: Son beş yılın kâr artışı yükselen faizlerin ve yüksek piyasa oynaklığının dönemine denk geldi. Hacimler normale dönerse hem büyüme hem kârlılık geriler; beş yıl tam bir döngüyü göstermez.

2026'nın ilk yarısında faaliyet kârı artmadı (88,0 milyon frank; 88,2). Net kârdaki %12,6'lık artış iştirak katkısından, düşük kur zararından ve düşük vergiden geldi. Geçen yılın ilk yarısında ayrıca İngiltere'de kaybedilen bir davanın 8,0 milyon franklık gideri vardı.
2025'in ikinci yarısındaki kârda tek seferlik bir kazanç var: Gaitame.com'un bir bağlı ortaklığını satmasından vergi sonrası 5,9 milyon frank. Son 12 ayın kârı bu kadar yüksek görünüyor.
Gelirin çoğu dolar, sterlin, avro ve yenle kazanılıyor; frank güçlenince kâr düşüyor (2026 ilk yarı gelir: sabit kurla +%11,0, frankla +%3,1). Enflasyon düzeltmesi İsviçre enflasyonuyla yapıldı.

Hukuki ve bilanço dışı riskler: yaptırımlar yüzünden takası yapılamayan ruble cinsi menkul kıymet işlemlerinden 15,8 milyon franklık alacak duruyor; karşılıklar 23,9 milyon frank. Kontrol tek ortakta (%68,94) ve opsiyonlar payı yaklaşık %5 seyreltiyor.

en.one: Global interdealer broker for interest-rate, currency and commodity trades between banks. The moat is narrow: scale and network are real, but profit depends on market volatility and on brokers.
en.business: Compagnie Financière Tradition brokers interest-rate, currency, bond, equity-derivative and commodity trades between banks and institutions and earns a commission on each trade. It works in more than 30 countries and had 2,470 staff at the end of 2025. In 2025 revenue including joint ventures was 1,203.6 million francs and operating profit 187.4 million francs. Gaitame.com, a retail currency-trading business in Japan, is a joint venture. Staff costs are about 69% of revenue (771.2 million francs; revenue 1,115.8 million).
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The advantage comes from scale and network: trades go to the broker where most buyers and sellers already meet. The company describes itself as one of the few truly global players in its industry. It shows in the numbers: operating margin including joint ventures was 13.4% in 2024, 15.6% in 2025 and 16.8% in the first half of 2026; real return on equity rose from 15.4% to 27.9% over five years and is 28.8% for the last 12 months. Weak points: about 69% of revenue goes to staff, so much of the earnings power sits with the brokers; volumes depend on interest rates and volatility; electronic platforms pressure voice broking. No market-share figure is in the documents read. So the moat is narrow, not wide.
en.mgmt: The company is controlled by VIEL & Cie, with 68.94% of the capital. No other shareholder has more than 3% of the votes. Profit goes to dividends, buybacks and equity: a dividend of 7.50 francs per share for 2025 (up 11.1%; 57.1 million francs paid on 28 May 2026); 114,238 shares were bought back in 2025 for 26.9 million francs (about 236 francs a share) and 142,183 shares were cancelled. At 30 June 2026 there were 7,965,636 shares in issue, 363,988 of them held by the company. A flaw: 373,605 share options were outstanding at the end of 2025 (about 4.7% of issued shares); diluted earnings per share are about 5% below basic (first half of 2026: 9.95 and 10.43 francs). Share-based pay expense is small: 2.0 million francs in 2025 and 2.1 million in the first half of 2026. Goodwill is 34.3 million francs, 7% of parent equity; no impairment in the last two years. Recurring restructuring charges were looked for and are not in the documents read.
en.latest: 28 August 2026: The company reported profit attributable to shareholders of 79.1 million francs for the first half of 2026 (70.2 million a year earlier; +12.6%, +22.5% at constant exchange rates). Earnings per share were 10.43 francs (9.14); diluted 9.95 francs (8.80). Revenue was 597.8 million francs (+3.1%; +11.0% at constant rates). Operating profit was flat at 88.0 million francs (88.2); the margin was 14.7% (15.2%). The rise came from below the operating line: the share of associates and joint ventures rose from 12.1 million francs to 16.1 million, currency losses shrank, and the tax rate fell from 26.1% to 23.4%. Equity attributable to shareholders was 493.3 million francs. The company gave no numerical outlook.
risks: The profit growth of the last five years coincided with rising interest rates and high market volatility. If volumes normalise, both growth and profitability fall back; five years do not show a full cycle.

Operating profit did not grow in the first half of 2026 (88.0 million francs; 88.2). The 12.6% rise in net profit came from associates, lower currency losses and a lower tax rate. The first half of last year also carried an 8.0 million franc charge for a lawsuit lost in England.
Profit in the second half of 2025 includes a one-off gain: 5.9 million francs after tax from Gaitame.com selling a subsidiary. The profit of the last 12 months is higher by that amount.

Most revenue is earned in dollars, sterling, euros and yen; profit falls when the franc strengthens (first-half 2026 revenue: +11.0% at constant rates, +3.1% in francs). The inflation adjustment uses Swiss inflation.

Legal and off-balance-sheet risks: receivables of 15.8 million francs remain from rouble-denominated securities trades that cannot settle because of sanctions; provisions are 23.9 million francs. Control sits with one shareholder (68.94%) and options dilute shareholders by about 5%.

The first half of last year carried an 8.0 million franc lawsuit charge. The lowest, after inflation, is 12.4%. That is not less than half the formula's rate; the rate was not lowered.

BCHN.one: Pistonlu kompresör sistemleri yapan ve kurulu makinelere servis veren şirket. Hendek dar ve servis kolunda; sipariş düştü, satış ve kâr bu yıl geriliyor.
BCHN.business: Burckhardt Compression rafineri, petrokimya, gaz taşıma ve depolama, hidrojen ve endüstriyel gaz tesisleri için pistonlu kompresör sistemleri yapar, sonra bu makinelere yedek parça ve servis verir. Mali yıl mart sonunda biter. Mart 2026'da biten yılda satış 1.057,1 milyon frank, faaliyet kârı 141,0 milyon frank oldu. Sistemler kolu 738,6 milyon frank satışla 79,2 milyon frank (marj %10,7), Servis kolu 318,5 milyon frank satışla 77,7 milyon frank (marj %24,4) faaliyet kârı getirdi.
BCHN.moat_text: Hendek dar ve Servis kolunda. Kurulu makine sayısı yıllarca yedek parça ve bakım işi getirir: Servis kolunun brüt marjı %47, faaliyet marjı %21,6-24,4. Bu kol satışın %30'unu, kol kârının yaklaşık yarısını verir. Sistemler kolu proje işidir, teklifle alınır; marjı ilk kez çift haneye çıktı (%10,7). Şirketin brüt marjı son üç dönemde %28,0-28,8 arasında kaldı. Reel özsermaye kârlılığı beş yılda %18,5'ten %29,5'e çıktı, son 12 ayda %30,6. Dikkat: şirket Swiss GAAP FER uyguluyor ve şerefiyeyi özsermayeden düşüyor; bu, özsermaye kârlılığını bir miktar yüksek gösterir (şerefiye dahil özsermaye 370,8 milyon frank; 361,2). Zayıf yan: sistem siparişi büyük projelere bağlı ve bir yılda %42 düşebildi. Pazar payı rakamı okunan belgelerde yok. Bu yüzden geniş değil, dar.
BCHN.mgmt: Kâr temettüye ve küçük, ana işle ilgili satın almalara gidiyor. Temettü hisse başına 18,00 frank (dağıtım oranı %55,2; politika %50-70). Net finansal pozisyon artıda: 31 Mart 2026'da 110,8 milyon frank net nakit. Satın almalar küçük ve servis işiyle ilgili: ABD'li yedek parça üreticisi ACT için 10,5 milyon frank (Eylül 2025); Fornovo Gas Temmuz 2026'da alındı, bedeli okunan belgelerde yok. 3.400.000 hisse var; 31 Mart 2026'da 27.939'u şirketin elindeydi. Hisse bazlı ücret 5,5 milyon frank (kârın %5,0'ı); seyreltme yok (temel ve seyreltilmiş hisse başına kâr aynı). Ağustos 2026'da yaklaşık 220 kişilik işten çıkarma açıklandı; tek seferlik gider 3,4 milyon frank, hedeflenen yıllık tasarruf 20 milyon frank. Emeklilik fonları fazla veriyor (%127,6 ve %131,2). Büyük ortaklara bakıldı, okunan bölümlerde yok.
BCHN.latest: 3 Kasım 2026: Şirket nisan-eylül 2026 dönemini açıkladı. Sipariş 422,5 milyon frank (+%5,4). Satış 459,0 milyon frank (−%11,1). Faaliyet kârı 55,5 milyon frank (geçen yıl 65,5 milyon; −%15,4), marj %12,1 (%12,7); 3,4 milyon franklık yeniden yapılanma gideri hariç marj %12,8. Net kâr 43,0 milyon frank (48,7 milyon; yaklaşık −%12). Servis kolunun marjı %23,9'dan %21,6'ya indi. Şirket Mart 2027'de bitecek yıl için beklentisini yineledi: 900-1.000 milyon frank satış, yaklaşık %12 faaliyet marjı. Bu, önceki yılın 1.057,1 milyon frank satışının ve %13,3 marjının altında.
risks: Kâr bu yıl geriliyor ve son 12 ayın kârı şirketin kendi beklentisinin üstünde duruyor. Beklenti (900-1.000 milyon frank satış, yaklaşık %12 marj) kabaca 108-120 milyon frank faaliyet kârı demek; önceki yıl 141,0 milyon franktı. Beklenti hisse başına kâr için verilmediğinden hesapta kullanılmadı.

Sipariş Mart 2026'da biten yılda %31,9 düştü (Sistemler kolunda %42,3). Şirket orta vadeli hedeflerine (1,2 milyar frank satış) ulaşma tarihini erteledi. İş döngüsel: müşteriler enerji, petrokimya ve gaz taşımacılığı yatırımcılarıdır; beş yıl tam bir döngüyü göstermez.
Servis kolunun marjı geriliyor (%24,7, %24,4, son yarıyılda %21,6). Hendek bu kolda olduğu için izlenmesi gereken ilk rakam budur.
Bilanço dışında 288,4 milyon franklık teminat var (özsermayenin yaklaşık %80'i); proje işinde olağandır ama bir projede sorun çıkarsa nakde döner.
Şerefiye özsermayeden düşüldüğü için özsermaye kârlılığı ve PD/DD bir miktar yüksek görünür. Satışların çoğu İsviçre dışında; enflasyon düzeltmesi İsviçre enflasyonuyla yapıldı.

en.one: Maker of reciprocating compressor systems that also services the installed machines. The moat is narrow and sits in services; orders fell, and sales and profit are declining this year.
en.business: Burckhardt Compression builds reciprocating compressor systems for refineries, petrochemicals, gas transport and storage, hydrogen and industrial gas plants, and then supplies spare parts and service for those machines. Its fiscal year ends in March. In the year to March 2026 sales were 1,057.1 million francs and operating profit 141.0 million francs. The Systems division earned 79.2 million francs on sales of 738.6 million (margin 10.7%); the Services division earned 77.7 million francs on sales of 318.5 million (margin 24.4%).
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow and sits in Services. The installed base brings spare-parts and maintenance work for years: Services has a gross margin of 47% and an operating margin of 21.6-24.4%. It provides 30% of sales and about half of divisional profit. Systems is project work won by bidding; its margin reached double digits for the first time (10.7%). The group's gross margin stayed between 28.0% and 28.8% over the last three periods. Real return on equity rose from 18.5% to 29.5% over five years and is 30.6% for the last 12 months. Note: the company uses Swiss GAAP FER and offsets goodwill against equity, which flatters return on equity somewhat (equity including goodwill 370.8 million francs; 361.2). Weak point: system orders depend on large projects and fell 42% in a single year. No market-share figure is in the documents read. So the moat is narrow, not wide.
en.mgmt: Profit goes to dividends and to small acquisitions related to the core business. The dividend is 18.00 francs per share (payout 55.2%; policy 50-70%). The net financial position is positive: net cash of 110.8 million francs at 31 March 2026. Acquisitions are small and tied to services: 10.5 million francs for the US spare-parts maker ACT (September 2025); Fornovo Gas was bought in July 2026, and its price is not in the documents read. There are 3,400,000 shares; 27,939 were held by the company at 31 March 2026. Share-based pay was 5.5 million francs (5.0% of profit); there is no dilution (basic and diluted earnings per share are the same). In August 2026 about 220 job cuts were announced; the one-off cost is 3.4 million francs and the targeted saving 20 million francs a year. The pension funds are over-funded (127.6% and 131.2%). en.latest: 3 November 2026: The company reported April-September 2026. Orders were 422.5 million francs (+5.4%). Sales were 459.0 million francs (−11.1%). Operating profit was 55.5 million francs (65.5 million a year earlier; −15.4%), a margin of 12.1% (12.7%); excluding 3.4 million francs of restructuring costs the margin was 12.8%. Net profit was 43.0 million francs (48.7 million; about −12%). The Services margin fell from 23.9% to 21.6%. The company confirmed its outlook for the year to March 2027: sales of 900-1,000 million francs and an operating margin of about 12%. That is below the previous year's sales of 1,057.1 million francs and margin of 13.3%.
risks: Profit is falling this year, and the profit of the last 12 months stands above the company's own outlook. The outlook (sales of 900-1,000 million francs, margin of about 12%) means roughly 108-120 million francs of operating profit; the previous year's was 141.0 million. Because the outlook is not given for earnings per share, it was not used in the calculation.

Orders fell 31.9% in the year to March 2026 (42.3% in Systems). The company has delayed the date for reaching its mid-range targets (sales of 1.2 billion francs). The business is cyclical: customers are investors in energy, petrochemicals and gas shipping; five years do not show a full cycle.
The Services margin is slipping (24.7%, 24.4%, and 21.6% in the latest half). Since the moat sits in this division, it is the first number to watch.
Off the balance sheet there are guarantees of 288.4 million francs (about 80% of equity); this is normal in project work but turns into cash if a project goes wrong.
Because goodwill is offset against equity, return on equity and price-to-book look somewhat high. Most sales are outside Switzerland; the inflation adjustment uses Swiss inflation.

en.one: Maker of vacuum measurement, gas analysis and leak detection instruments. The moat is narrow; more than half of sales depend on the semiconductor cycle, and profit is at a good point in that cycle.
en.business: INFICON makes measurement and control instruments, gas analysers and leak detectors for production processes that run under vacuum. Its customers are makers of semiconductor and coating equipment, general vacuum users, and refrigeration, air-conditioning and automotive manufacturers. The company reports in US dollars. In 2025 sales were 673.7 million dollars and operating income 112.3 million dollars. 49% of sales came from semiconductor and vacuum coating and 25.9% from general vacuum; in the third quarter of 2026 the semiconductor share rose to 58%.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The instruments are built into the customer's production line and recipe; replacing them is costly and risky. It shows in gross margin: 47.1% in 2024 and 50.1% in the third quarter of 2026. Real return on equity did not fall below 21% in any of the five years (31.8%, 29.8%, 32.0%, 30.5%, 21.1%; 22.7% for the last 12 months) and the company holds net cash. But pricing power has limits: in 2025 tariffs and the cost of relocating production cut gross margin to 44.9%, and to 43.0% in the third quarter; operating margin fell from 20.3% to 16.7%. The company could not pass the cost on at once. Half of sales depend on a small number of semiconductor equipment makers. No market-share figure is in the documents read. So the moat is narrow, not wide.
en.mgmt: The company has no net debt: net cash of 81.2 million dollars at the end of 2025 and an equity ratio of 74.1% (equity 426.4 million dollars). Profit goes to dividends and back into the business: a dividend of 2.00 francs per share for 2025 (payout about 73%); the rest to production investment such as the new plant in Malaysia. The documents read show no acquisitions and no buybacks. Share-based pay, goodwill, pension obligations and major shareholders were looked for and are not in the releases read (the 2025 annual report was not opened). On the data source's figures, about 69% of the last five years' profit turned into cash; the rest went into inventory and investment.
en.latest: 27 October 2026: The company reported third-quarter sales of 233.3 million dollars (+42.4%). Gross margin was 50.1% (43.0% a year earlier). Operating income was 59.5 million dollars (22.9 million), a margin of 25.5%. Net profit was 47.4 million dollars; earnings per share were 1.94 dollars (0.71). Semiconductor and vacuum coating sales rose 74.7%; sales to China rose 71.7% and were 31.4% of the total. The company said the quarter's margin included one-off positive effects, without giving the amount. It raised its 2026 guidance for the third time: sales of 820-850 million dollars and an operating margin of 21-22%.
risks: Profit depends on the semiconductor investment cycle and is at a good point in it: in the third quarter semiconductor sales rose 74.7% and operating margin reached 25.5%. In 2025 the same margin was 16.7%. This quarter's profit does not count as the normal earning power of the business.
The third-quarter margin includes one-off positive effects that the company did not quantify; the profit of the last 12 months is higher by that amount.
China is 31.4% of sales. Export controls or local rivals could cut that share quickly. In 2025 tariffs lowered the margin markedly; the company says logistics and material costs are rising again.

The company reports in dollars and the share trades in francs; if the dollar weakens, profit and dividend fall in franc terms. The inflation adjustment uses Swiss inflation, although most sales are in Asia and the Americas.
Share-based pay, goodwill and pension obligations could not be read from a document in this run (the annual report was not opened).

en.one: Distributor that sells fasteners to industrial companies and manages their stock flow. The moat is narrow; profit follows the industrial cycle, and debt rose with an acquisition.
en.business: Bossard sells fasteners such as screws, nuts and rivets to industrial customers; alongside, it gives engineering advice and runs the stock flow in the customer's factory with its own systems. In 2025 sales were 1,068.9 million francs, operating profit 106.6 million francs and net income 74.6 million francs. 646.9 million francs of sales came from Europe, 228.6 million from America and 193.4 million from Asia. In January 2025 it bought the German distributor Ferdinand Gross for 61.5 million francs.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The product is an ordinary part; the advantage comes from service: the company ties the supply and stock tracking of thousands of small parts into the customer's line, and switching supplier is a chore for the customer. It shows in a margin that is high for a distributor: gross margin was 32.3% in 2025 and 34.4% in the first half of 2026; operating margin 10.0% and 12.7%. Real return on equity fell from 27.3% to 19.0% over five years and is 21.6% for the last 12 months. Note: the company uses Swiss GAAP FER and offsets goodwill against equity. Had goodwill been amortised, 2025 operating profit would have been 81.9 million francs, not 106.6 million; return on equity looks high for that reason. Return on invested capital is more modest at 12-13%. There are large rivals, and a customer can buy the part elsewhere if it wishes. So the moat is narrow, not wide.
en.mgmt: Control sits with the Kolin Group (the Bossard families): 56.4% of the votes and 28.0% of the capital entitled to dividends. There are two share classes: 6,650,000 listed A shares (nominal 5 francs) and 6,750,000 B shares (nominal 1 franc); minority shareholders have limited say. About 40% of profit is paid as dividends (3.90 francs per share; earnings per A share 9.33 francs). The rest goes into working capital and acquisitions: with the Ferdinand Gross purchase net debt rose from 245.1 million francs to 311.3 million. The purchase is in the core business. The company holds 292,710 of its own A shares. Share-based pay is small: 1.6 million francs (2% of profit). There is no pension deficit; off-balance-sheet guarantees are 1.2 million francs. Recurring one-off charges were looked for and are not in the documents.
en.latest: 21 July 2026: The company reported first-half 2026 sales of 575.7 million francs (+5.3%; +9.7% in local currency). Gross margin was 34.4% (32.5% a year earlier). Operating profit was 72.9 million francs (55.5 million), a margin of 12.7% (10.2%). Net income was 54.7 million francs (38.7 million; +41.3%). Net debt was 317.3 million francs; net debt to EBITDA 2.1 (2.8 a year earlier). Free cash flow was 24.6 million francs. For 2026 the company expects organic growth of over 5% a year and higher profitability than last year; it gave no profit figure.
risks: Profit follows industrial output: in 2025 organic growth was only 2.0%, organic sales in Europe fell 1.6% and net income slipped (74.6 million francs; 75.3). The 41.3% rise in the first half of 2026 comes from that low base.

Net debt is 317.3 million francs, 2.1 times EBITDA; the data source's ratio is 2.24, not far from the threshold (3.0). Inventory of 371.1 million francs is more than a third of sales; if demand falls, cash stays tied up in stock.
Because goodwill is offset against equity, return on equity and price-to-book look high: had goodwill been amortised, 2025 operating profit would have been 81.9 million francs.
Two share classes: the Kolin Group holds 56.4% of the votes with 28.0% of the capital.

About 40% of sales are outside Europe and most are outside Switzerland; profit falls when the franc strengthens (first-half sales: +9.7% in local currency, +5.3% in francs). en.one: Group that installs electrical, heating, ventilation and plumbing systems in Swiss buildings. Work is won by offer and margins are thin; it did not pass the moat test.
en.business: Burkhalter, through local companies in many parts of Switzerland, installs and maintains electrical systems, heating, ventilation, air conditioning and plumbing in buildings. In 2025 sales were 1,207.6 million francs, operating profit 73.8 million francs and group profit 61.3 million francs. The group grows by buying small local installers: two in 2025 and six in the first eight months of 2026.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak. The work is installation work won by offer from building owners and contractors; rivals are many and price decides. It shows in the margin: operating margin was 5.9% in 2024 and 6.1% in 2025. The advantages are scale and local reputation; maintenance and repair work recurs to a degree. Real return on equity is very high (from 30.9% to 44.6% over five years; 58.9% for the last 12 months), but that comes from a business model needing little capital and from small equity, not from pricing power: the company pays out almost all its profit and price-to-book is 13.8. With a B score of 1 the company did not pass Wall 3.
en.mgmt: Most profit is paid out as dividends: 5.20 francs per share for 2025 (earnings per share 5.78 francs; about 90%), half of it from capital contribution reserves. Growth continues through purchases of small local companies; prices are not in the releases read. On the data source's figures the share count rose 77% in five years; the reason could not be read from a company document in this run. Share-based pay, the amount of goodwill, pension obligations and major shareholders were looked for and are not in the releases read (the 2025 financial report could not be opened).

en.one: Out-of-home advertising company that runs street, station and transport advertising sites in Switzerland. The moat is narrow and tied to concession contracts; more than all of profit is paid out as dividends.
en.business: APG|SGA rents advertising sites from cities, transport companies and private owners and sells the posters and digital screens on them to advertisers. In 2025 advertising revenue was 327.0 million francs; 312.9 million came from Switzerland and 14.2 million from Alma Quattro in Serbia. Operating profit was 33.2 million francs (margin 10.1%) and net income 27.1 million francs. The company holds net cash: 53.0 million francs at the end of 2025.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The advantage comes from a nationwide network of sites and from long concession contracts: the SBB contract, covering third-party advertising at all Swiss railway stations, was renewed to 2030. For an advertiser wanting a national campaign, a match for this network is not easily built. But the sites do not belong to the company; contracts are tendered again when they expire, and much of the revenue goes to the site owners as rent. Operating margin is modest for that reason: 11.0% in 2024 and 10.1% in 2025. Real return on equity rose from 11.6% to 34.9% over five years and is 52.2% for the last 12 months; part of that height comes from small equity (72.9 million francs; all profit is paid out). No market-share figure is in the documents read. So the moat is narrow, not wide.
en.mgmt: More than all of profit is paid out: a dividend of 12 francs per share for 2025, against earnings per share of 9.03 francs. The gap is paid from net cash; that cannot go on for ever. The shareholder base is changing: in December 2025 NZZ announced it would raise its stake from 25% to 45% by buying shares from JCDecaux and Pargesa at 220 francs a share; completion could not be confirmed in the documents read. The documents read show no buybacks and no share issues. In August 2026 the company sold its building in Bern (effect on net result about 3.4 million francs); 2024 also carried a 2.9 million franc gain on a property sale, so such gains recur but are not profit of the business. From 1 January 2027 the poster sites of ESH Médias will be taken over; the price is not in the documents read. Share-based pay, goodwill and pension obligations were looked for and are not in the documents read (the annual report was not opened).
en.latest: 24 July 2026: The company reported first-half 2026 advertising revenue of 163.6 million francs (+10.4%; Switzerland +11.0%, international −0.5%). EBITDA was 22.7 million francs (+14.9%) and operating profit 18.6 million francs (+24.9%). Net income was 15.2 million francs (12.1 million a year earlier; +24.9%); earnings per share were 5.05 francs (4.05). Excluding one-time effects, net income was 14.4 million francs. Free cash flow was 5.0 million francs. On 21 August 2026 the company announced it had signed a contract to sell its building in Bern: a positive effect of about 3.4 million francs on the net result and a cash inflow of 10.4 million francs from investing activities.
risks: The dividend is above profit (12 francs; earnings per share 9.03 francs) and is paid from net cash. The calculation assumes no growth because no profit is retained; if the dividend falls to the level of profit, the yield falls too.
Revenue depends on a few large concession contracts; the most important, with SBB, ends in 2030. If it is not renewed, or is renewed at a higher rent, profit falls permanently.

Profit in the second half of 2026 will include a one-off gain of about 3.4 million francs from the sale of the Bern building; the first half also has a one-time positive effect of 0.7 million francs.
The shareholder base is changing (NZZ's stake is rising to 45%) and arbitration against the Serbian state continues; revenue in Serbia fell 6.5%.
